**Note:** The returned value is multiplied by a factor of `1000000` to preserve 6 digits of precision. It must be divided by `1000000.0` to convert the value to a floating point number.

LIMIT_METALFX_TEMPORAL_SCALER_MIN_SCALE.description:
Returns the smallest value for `ProjectSettings.rendering/scaling_3d/scale` when using the MetalFX temporal upscaler.

**Note:** The returned value is multiplied by a factor of `1000000` to preserve 6 digits of precision. It must be divided by `1000000.0` to convert the value to a floating point number.

LOGIC_OP_AND_INVERTED.description: AND logic operation with the *source* operand being inverted. See also `LOGIC_OP_AND_REVERSE`.

LOGIC_OP_AND_REVERSE.description: AND logic operation with the *destination* operand being inverted. See also `LOGIC_OP_AND_INVERTED`.

LOGIC_OP_CLEAR.description: Clear logic operation (result is always `0`). See also `LOGIC_OP_SET`.

LOGIC_OP_COPY.description: Copy logic operation (keeps the *source* value as-is). See also `LOGIC_OP_COPY_INVERTED` and `LOGIC_OP_NO_OP`.

LOGIC_OP_COPY_INVERTED.description: NOT logic operation (inverts the value). See also `LOGIC_OP_COPY`.

LOGIC_OP_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `LogicOperation` enum.

LOGIC_OP_NO_OP.description: No-op logic operation (keeps the *destination* value as-is). See also `LOGIC_OP_COPY`.

LOGIC_OP_OR_INVERTED.description: OR logic operation with the *source* operand being inverted. See also `LOGIC_OP_OR_REVERSE`.

LOGIC_OP_OR_REVERSE.description: OR logic operation with the *destination* operand being inverted. See also `LOGIC_OP_OR_REVERSE`.

LOGIC_OP_SET.description: SET logic operation (result is always `1`). See also `LOGIC_OP_CLEAR`.

MEMORY_TOTAL.description: Total memory taken. This is greater than the sum of `MEMORY_TEXTURES` and `MEMORY_BUFFERS`, as it also includes miscellaneous memory usage.

NONE.description: No breadcrumb marker will be added.

OPAQUE_PASS.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"OPAQUE_PASS"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

POLYGON_CULL_BACK.description: Use polygon backface culling (faces pointing away from the camera are hidden).

POLYGON_CULL_DISABLED.description: Do not use polygon front face or backface culling.

POLYGON_CULL_FRONT.description: Use polygon frontface culling (faces pointing towards the camera are hidden).

POLYGON_FRONT_FACE_CLOCKWISE.description: Clockwise winding order to determine which face of a polygon is its front face.

POLYGON_FRONT_FACE_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE.description: Counter-clockwise winding order to determine which face of a polygon is its front face.

POST_PROCESSING_PASS.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"POST_PROCESSING_PASS"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

REFLECTION_PROBES.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"REFLECTION_PROBES"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_LINES.description: Line list rendering primitive. Lines are drawn separated from each other.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_LINESTRIPS.description: Line strip rendering primitive. Lines drawn are connected to the previous vertex.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_LINESTRIPS_WITH_ADJACEN.description:
[Line strip rendering primitive with adjacency.](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#drawing-line-strips-with-adjacency)

**Note:** Adjacency is only useful with geometry shaders, which Godot does not expose.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_LINES_WITH_ADJACENCY.description:
[Line list rendering primitive with adjacency.](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#drawing-line-lists-with-adjacency)

**Note:** Adjacency is only useful with geometry shaders, which Godot does not expose.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `RenderPrimitive` enum.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_POINTS.description: Point rendering primitive (with constant size, regardless of distance from camera).

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TESSELATION_PATCH.description: Tessellation patch rendering primitive. Only useful with tessellation shaders, which can be used to deform these patches.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES.description: Triangle list rendering primitive. Triangles are drawn separated from each other.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES_WITH_ADJACENC.description:
[Triangle list rendering primitive with adjacency.](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#drawing-triangle-lists-with-adjacency)

**Note:** Adjacency is only useful with geometry shaders, which Godot does not expose.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS.description: Triangle strip rendering primitive. Triangles drawn are connected to the previous triangle.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS_WITH_AJ.description:
[Triangle strip rendering primitive with adjacency.](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#drawing-triangle-strips-with-adjacency)

**Note:** Adjacency is only useful with geometry shaders, which Godot does not expose.

RENDER_PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS_WITH_RE.description:
Triangle strip rendering primitive with *primitive restart* enabled. Triangles drawn are connected to the previous triangle, but a primitive restart index can be specified before drawing to create a second triangle strip after the specified index.

**Note:** Only compatible with indexed draws.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_FLOAT_OPAQUE_BLACK.description: Return a floating-point opaque black color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_FLOAT_OPAQUE_WHITE.description: Return a floating-point opaque white color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_FLOAT_TRANSPARENT_B.description: Return a floating-point transparent black color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_INT_OPAQUE_BLACK.description: Return an integer opaque black color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_INT_OPAQUE_WHITE.description: Return an integer opaque white color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_INT_TRANSPARENT_BLA.description: Return an integer transparent black color when sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range. Only effective if the sampler repeat mode is `SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER`.

SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `SamplerBorderColor` enum.

SAMPLER_FILTER_LINEAR.description: Bilinear sampler filtering. Sampling at higher resolutions than the source will result in a blurry look.

SAMPLER_FILTER_NEAREST.description: Nearest-neighbor sampler filtering. Sampling at higher resolutions than the source will result in a pixelated look.

SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER.description: Sample with repeating disabled. When sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range, return the specified `RDSamplerState.border_color`.

SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_CLAMP_TO_EDGE.description: Sample with repeating disabled. When sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range, return the color of the last pixel on the edge.

SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `SamplerRepeatMode` enum.

SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_MIRRORED_REPEAT.description: Sample with mirrored repeating enabled. When sampling outside the `[0.0, 1.0]` range, return a mirrored version of the sampler. This mirrored version is mirrored again if sampling further away, with the pattern repeating indefinitely.

SAMPLER_REPEAT_MODE_MIRROR_CLAMP_TO_EDGE.description: Sample with mirrored repeating enabled, but only once. When sampling in the `[-1.0, 0.0]` range, return a mirrored version of the sampler. When sampling outside the `[-1.0, 1.0]` range, return the color of the last pixel on the edge.

SHADER_LANGUAGE_GLSL.description: Khronos' GLSL shading language (used natively by OpenGL and Vulkan). This is the language used for core Godot shaders.

SHADER_LANGUAGE_HLSL.description: Microsoft's High-Level Shading Language (used natively by Direct3D, but can also be used in Vulkan).

SHADER_STAGE_ANY_HIT.description: Any hit shader stage. Invoked when ray intersections are not opaque. This can be used to specify what happens when a ray hits any of the geometry in the scene.

SHADER_STAGE_ANY_HIT_BIT.description: Any hit shader stage bit (see also `SHADER_STAGE_ANY_HIT`).

SHADER_STAGE_CLOSEST_HIT.description: Closest hit shader stage. This can be used to specify what happens when a ray hits the closest geometry in the scene.

SHADER_STAGE_CLOSEST_HIT_BIT.description: Closest hit shader stage bit (see also `SHADER_STAGE_CLOSEST_HIT`).

SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE.description: Compute shader stage. This can be used to run arbitrary computing tasks in a shader, performing them on the GPU instead of the CPU.

SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT.description: Fragment shader stage (called "pixel shader" in Direct3D). This can be used to manipulate pixels from a shader.

SHADER_STAGE_INTERSECTION.description: Intersection shader stage. The intersection shader for triangles is built-in. This can be used to compute ray intersections with primitives that are not triangles.

SHADER_STAGE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ShaderStage` enum.

SHADER_STAGE_MISS.description: Miss shader stage. This can be used to specify what happens if a ray does not hit anything in the scene.

SHADER_STAGE_RAYGEN.description: Ray generation shader stage. This can be used to generate primary rays.

SHADER_STAGE_RAYGEN_BIT.description: Ray generation shader stage bit (see also `SHADER_STAGE_RAYGEN`).

SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_CONTROL.description: Tessellation control shader stage. This can be used to create additional geometry from a shader.

SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_CONTROL_BIT.description: Tessellation control shader stage bit (see also `SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_CONTROL`).

SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_EVALUATION.description: Tessellation evaluation shader stage. This can be used to create additional geometry from a shader.

SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_EVALUATION_BIT.description: Tessellation evaluation shader stage bit (see also `SHADER_STAGE_TESSELATION_EVALUATION`).

SHADER_STAGE_VERTEX.description: Vertex shader stage. This can be used to manipulate vertices from a shader (but not create new vertices).

SHADOW_PASS_CUBE.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"SHADOW_PASS_CUBE"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

SHADOW_PASS_DIRECTIONAL.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"SHADOW_PASS_DIRECTIONAL"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

SKY_PASS.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"SKY_PASS"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_CLAMP.description: Decrement the existing stencil value and clamp to the minimum value if reached. Stencil bits are considered as an unsigned integer.

STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_WRAP.description: Decrement the stencil value and wrap around to the maximum representable unsigned if reaching the minimum. Stencil bits are considered as an unsigned integer.

STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_CLAMP.description: Increment the existing stencil value and clamp to the maximum representable unsigned value if reached. Stencil bits are considered as an unsigned integer.

STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_WRAP.description: Increment the stencil value and wrap around to `0` if reaching the maximum representable unsigned. Stencil bits are considered as an unsigned integer.

STENCIL_OP_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `StencilOperation` enum.

STENCIL_OP_REPLACE.description: Replace the existing stencil value with the new one.

SUPPORTS_BUFFER_DEVICE_ADDRESS.description: Features support for buffer device address extension.

SUPPORTS_HDR_OUTPUT.description: Support for high dynamic range (HDR) output.

SUPPORTS_RAYTRACING_PIPELINE.description:
Support for raytracing pipeline extension.

**Note:** This is currently only supported when using Vulkan. This is not supported on macOS and iOS (even on hardware supporting raytracing) due to MoltenVK limitations.

SUPPORTS_RAY_QUERY.description:
Support for ray query extension.

**Note:** This is currently only supported when using Vulkan. This is not supported on macOS and iOS (even on hardware supporting raytracing) due to MoltenVK limitations.

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_1.description: Perform 1 texture sample (this is the fastest but lowest-quality for antialiasing).

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_16.description: Perform 16 texture samples. Not supported on mobile GPUs and many desktop GPUs.

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_32.description: Perform 32 texture samples. Not supported on most GPUs.

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_64.description: Perform 64 texture samples (this is the slowest but highest-quality for antialiasing). Not supported on most GPUs.

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_8.description: Perform 8 texture samples. Not supported on mobile GPUs (including Apple Silicon).

TEXTURE_SAMPLES_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `TextureSamples` enum.

TEXTURE_SWIZZLE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `TextureSwizzle` enum.

TEXTURE_TYPE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `TextureType` enum.

TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_FROM_BIT.description: Texture can be a source for `texture_copy`.

TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_TO_BIT.description: Texture can be a destination for `texture_copy`.

TEXTURE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT.description: Texture can be used as a color attachment in a framebuffer.

TEXTURE_USAGE_CPU_READ_BIT.description: Texture can be read back on the CPU using `texture_get_data` faster than without this bit, since it is always kept in the system memory.

TEXTURE_USAGE_DEPTH_RESOLVE_ATTACHMENT_B.description: Texture can be used as a depth/stencil resolve attachment in a framebuffer.

TEXTURE_USAGE_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_B.description: Texture can be used as a depth/stencil attachment in a framebuffer.

TEXTURE_USAGE_INPUT_ATTACHMENT_BIT.description: Texture can be used as a [input attachment](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#descriptorsets-inputattachment) in a framebuffer.

TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT.description: Texture can be used as a [storage image](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#descriptorsets-storageimage) with support for atomic operations.

TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_BIT.description: Texture can be used as a [storage image](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/html/vkspec.html#descriptorsets-storageimage).

TRANSPARENT_PASS.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"TRANSPARENT_PASS"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

UI_PASS.description: During a GPU crash in dev or debug mode, Godot's error message will include `"UI_PASS"` for added context as to when the crash occurred.

UNIFORM_TYPE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `UniformType` enum.

UNIFORM_TYPE_SAMPLER_WITH_TEXTURE_BUFFER.description: Sampler uniform with a texture buffer.

UNIFORM_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER_DYNAMIC.description:
Same as UNIFORM_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER but for buffers created with BUFFER_CREATION_DYNAMIC_PERSISTENT_BIT.

**Note:** This flag is not available to GD users due to being too dangerous (i.e. wrong usage can result in visual glitches).

It's exposed in case GD users receive a buffer created with such flag from Godot.

UNIFORM_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_DYNAMIC.description:
Same as UNIFORM_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER but for buffers created with BUFFER_CREATION_DYNAMIC_PERSISTENT_BIT.

**Note:** This flag is not available to GD users due to being too dangerous (i.e. wrong usage can result in visual glitches).

It's exposed in case GD users receive a buffer created with such flag from Godot.

VERTEX_FREQUENCY_INSTANCE.description: Vertex attribute addressing is a function of the instance index. This is used to specify the rate at which vertex attributes are pulled from buffers.

VERTEX_FREQUENCY_VERTEX.description: Vertex attribute addressing is a function of the vertex. This is used to specify the rate at which vertex attributes are pulled from buffers.

RenderingDevice.description:
`RenderingDevice` is an abstraction for working with modern low-level graphics APIs such as Vulkan. Compared to `RenderingServer` (which works with Godot's own rendering subsystems), `RenderingDevice` is much lower-level and allows working more directly with the underlying graphics APIs. `RenderingDevice` is used in Godot to provide support for several modern low-level graphics APIs while reducing the amount of code duplication required. `RenderingDevice` can also be used in your own projects to perform things that are not exposed by `RenderingServer` or high-level nodes, such as using compute shaders.

On startup, Godot creates a global `RenderingDevice` which can be retrieved using `RenderingServer.get_rendering_device`. This global `RenderingDevice` performs drawing to the screen.

**Local RenderingDevices:** Using `RenderingServer.create_local_rendering_device`, you can create "secondary" rendering devices to perform drawing and GPU compute operations on separate threads.

**Note:** `RenderingDevice` assumes intermediate knowledge of modern graphics APIs such as Vulkan, Direct3D 12, Metal or WebGPU. These graphics APIs are lower-level than OpenGL or Direct3D 11, requiring you to perform what was previously done by the graphics driver itself. If you have difficulty understanding the concepts used in this class, follow the [Vulkan Tutorial](https://vulkan-tutorial.com/) or [Vulkan Guide](https://vkguide.dev/). It's recommended to have existing modern OpenGL or Direct3D 11 knowledge before attempting to learn a low-level graphics API.

**Note:** `RenderingDevice` is not available when running in headless mode or when using the Compatibility rendering method.

ARRAY_COLOR.description: Array is a vertex color array.

ARRAY_COMPRESS_FLAGS_BASE.description: Shift of first compress flag. Compress flags should be passed to `ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays` and `SurfaceTool.commit`.

ARRAY_CUSTOM0.description: Array is a custom data array for the first set of custom data.

ARRAY_CUSTOM1.description: Array is a custom data array for the second set of custom data.

ARRAY_CUSTOM2.description: Array is a custom data array for the third set of custom data.

ARRAY_CUSTOM3.description: Array is a custom data array for the fourth set of custom data.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_COUNT.description: The number of custom data arrays available (`ARRAY_CUSTOM0`, `ARRAY_CUSTOM1`, `ARRAY_CUSTOM2`, `ARRAY_CUSTOM3`).

ARRAY_CUSTOM_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ArrayCustomFormat` enum.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM.description: Custom data array contains 8-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are normalized, signed floating-point in the `[-1.0, 1.0]` range.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM.description: Custom data array contains 8-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are normalized, unsigned floating-point in the `[0.0, 1.0]` range.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_FLOAT.description: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF.description: Custom data array contains 16-bit-per-channel red/green/blue/alpha color data. Values are floating-point in half precision.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGB_FLOAT.description: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green/blue color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_FLOAT.description: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red/green color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF.description: Custom data array contains 16-bit-per-channel red/green color data. Values are floating-point in half precision.

ARRAY_CUSTOM_R_FLOAT.description: Custom data array contains 32-bit-per-channel red color data. Values are floating-point in single precision.

ARRAY_FLAG_COMPRESS_ATTRIBUTES.description: Flag used to mark that a mesh is using compressed attributes (vertices, normals, tangents, UVs). When this form of compression is enabled, vertex positions will be packed into an RGBA16UNORM attribute and scaled in the vertex shader. The normal and tangent will be packed into an RG16UNORM representing an axis, and a 16-bit float stored in the A-channel of the vertex. UVs will use 16-bit normalized floats instead of full 32-bit signed floats. When using this compression mode you must use either vertices, normals, and tangents or only vertices. You cannot use normals without tangents. Importers will automatically enable this compression if they can.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_CURRENT_VERSION.description: Flag used to record the current version that the engine expects. Currently this is the same as `ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_2`.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_1.description: Flag used to record the format used by prior mesh versions before the introduction of a version.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_2.description: Flag used to record the second iteration of the mesh version flag. The primary difference between this and `ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_1` is that this version supports `ARRAY_FLAG_COMPRESS_ATTRIBUTES` and in this version vertex positions are de-interleaved from normals and tangents.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_BASE.description: Flag used to mark the start of the bits used to store the mesh version.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_MASK.description: Flag used to isolate the bits used for mesh version after using `ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_SHIFT` to shift them into place.

ARRAY_FLAG_FORMAT_VERSION_SHIFT.description: Flag used to shift a mesh format int to bring the version into the lowest digits.

ARRAY_FLAG_USES_EMPTY_VERTEX_ARRAY.description: Flag used to mark that the mesh does not have a vertex array and instead will infer vertex positions in the shader using indices and other information.

ARRAY_FLAG_USE_2D_VERTICES.description: Flag used to mark that the array contains 2D vertices.

ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS.description: Flag used to mark that the array uses 8 bone weights instead of 4.

ARRAY_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_UPDATE.description: Flag used to mark that the mesh data will use `GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW` on GLES. Unused on Vulkan.

ARRAY_FORMAT_BLEND_SHAPE_MASK.description: Mask of mesh channels permitted in blend shapes.

ARRAY_FORMAT_BONES.description: Flag used to mark a bone information array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_COLOR.description: Flag used to mark a vertex color array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0.description: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the first set of custom data.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM0_SHIFT.description: Amount to shift `ArrayCustomFormat` for custom channel index 0.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1.description: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the second set of custom data.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM1_SHIFT.description: Amount to shift `ArrayCustomFormat` for custom channel index 1.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2.description: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the third set of custom data.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM2_SHIFT.description: Amount to shift `ArrayCustomFormat` for custom channel index 2.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3.description: Flag used to mark an array of custom per-vertex data for the fourth set of custom data.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM3_SHIFT.description: Amount to shift `ArrayCustomFormat` for custom channel index 3.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_BITS.description: Number of format bits per custom channel. See `ArrayCustomFormat`.

ARRAY_FORMAT_CUSTOM_MASK.description: Mask of custom format bits per custom channel. Must be shifted by one of the SHIFT constants. See `ArrayCustomFormat`.

ARRAY_FORMAT_INDEX.description: Flag used to mark an index array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_NORMAL.description: Flag used to mark a normal array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_TANGENT.description: Flag used to mark a tangent array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_TEX_UV.description: Flag used to mark a UV coordinates array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_TEX_UV2.description: Flag used to mark a UV coordinates array for the second UV coordinates.

ARRAY_FORMAT_VERTEX.description: Flag used to mark a vertex position array.

ARRAY_FORMAT_WEIGHTS.description: Flag used to mark a weights array.

ARRAY_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ArrayType` enum.

ARRAY_TEX_UV.description: Array is a UV coordinates array.

ARRAY_TEX_UV2.description: Array is a UV coordinates array for the second set of UV coordinates.

ARRAY_VERTEX.description: Array is a vertex position array.

BAKE_CHANNEL_ALBEDO_ALPHA.description: Index of `Image` in array of `Image`s returned by `bake_render_uv2`. Image uses `Image.FORMAT_RGBA8` and contains albedo color in the `.rgb` channels and alpha in the `.a` channel.

BAKE_CHANNEL_EMISSION.description: Index of `Image` in array of `Image`s returned by `bake_render_uv2`. Image uses `Image.FORMAT_RGBAH` and contains emission color in the `.rgb` channels and nothing in the `.a` channel.

BAKE_CHANNEL_NORMAL.description: Index of `Image` in array of `Image`s returned by `bake_render_uv2`. Image uses `Image.FORMAT_RGBA8` and contains the per-pixel normal of the object in the `.rgb` channels and nothing in the `.a` channel. The per-pixel normal is encoded as `normal * 0.5 + 0.5`.

BAKE_CHANNEL_ORM.description: Index of `Image` in array of `Image`s returned by `bake_render_uv2`. Image uses `Image.FORMAT_RGBA8` and contains ambient occlusion (from material and decals only) in the `.r` channel, roughness in the `.g` channel, metallic in the `.b` channel and sub surface scattering amount in the `.a` channel.

BLEND_SHAPE_MODE_RELATIVE.description: Blend shapes are relative to base weight.

CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_AND_DRAW.description: Parent is used for clipping child, but parent is also drawn underneath child as normal before clipping child to its visible area.

CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_CLIP_ONLY.description: Parent is used for the purposes of clipping only. Child is clipped to the parent's visible area, parent is not drawn.

CANVAS_GROUP_MODE_DISABLED.description: Child draws over parent and is not clipped.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_DEFAULT.description: Uses the default filter mode for this `Viewport`.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR.description: The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_M.description:
The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter` is `true`). This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance.

Use this for non-pixel art textures that may be viewed at a low scale (e.g. due to `Camera2D` zoom or sprite scaling), as mipmaps are important to smooth out pixels that are smaller than on-screen pixels.

The texture filter blends between the nearest 4 pixels and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter` is `true`) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look smooth from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

**Note:** This texture filter is rarely useful in 2D projects. `CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS` is usually more appropriate in this case.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST.description: The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel only. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and grainy from a distance (due to mipmaps not being sampled).

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_.description:
The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between the nearest 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter` is `true`). This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance.

Use this for non-pixel art textures that may be viewed at a low scale (e.g. due to `Camera2D` zoom or sprite scaling), as mipmaps are important to smooth out pixels that are smaller than on-screen pixels.

The texture filter reads from the nearest pixel and blends between 2 mipmaps (or uses the nearest mipmap if `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter` is `true`) based on the angle between the surface and the camera view. This makes the texture look pixelated from up close, and smooth from a distance. Anisotropic filtering improves texture quality on surfaces that are almost in line with the camera, but is slightly slower. The anisotropic filtering level can be changed by adjusting `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

**Note:** This texture filter is rarely useful in 2D projects. `CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST_WITH_MIPMAPS` is usually more appropriate in this case.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_DEFAULT.description: Uses the default repeat mode for this `Viewport`.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_DISABLED.description: Disables textures repeating. Instead, when reading UVs outside the 0-1 range, the value will be clamped to the edge of the texture, resulting in a stretched out look at the borders of the texture.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED.description: Enables the texture to repeat when UV coordinates are outside the 0-1 range. If using one of the linear filtering modes, this can result in artifacts at the edges of a texture when the sampler filters across the edges of the texture.

CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR.description: Flip the texture when repeating so that the edge lines up instead of abruptly changing.

CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MAX.description: The maximum Z-layer for canvas items.

CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MIN.description: The minimum Z-layer for canvas items.

CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_ADD.description: Adds light color additive to the canvas.

CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_MIX.description: The light adds color depending on transparency.

CANVAS_LIGHT_BLEND_MODE_SUB.description: Adds light color subtractive to the canvas.

CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_NONE.description: Do not apply a filter to canvas light shadows.

CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF13.description: Use PCF13 filtering to filter canvas light shadows.

CANVAS_LIGHT_FILTER_PCF5.description: Use PCF5 filtering to filter canvas light shadows.

CANVAS_OCCLUDER_POLYGON_CULL_CLOCKWISE.description: Culling of the canvas occluder is clockwise.

CANVAS_OCCLUDER_POLYGON_CULL_COUNTER_CLO.description: Culling of the canvas occluder is counterclockwise.

CANVAS_OCCLUDER_POLYGON_CULL_DISABLED.description: Culling of the canvas occluder is disabled.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_OPA.description: The callback is called after our opaque rendering pass, but before our sky is rendered.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_SKY.description: The callback is called after our sky is rendered, but before our back buffers are created (and if enabled, before subsurface scattering and/or screen space reflections).

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_TRA.description: The callback is called after our transparent rendering pass, but before any built-in post-processing effects and output to our render target.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_OPAQ.description: The callback is called before our opaque rendering pass, but after depth prepass (if applicable).

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_TRAN.description: The callback is called before our transparent rendering pass, but after our sky is rendered and we've created our back buffers.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_ACCESS_RESOLVED_C.description: The rendering effect requires the color buffer to be resolved if MSAA is enabled.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_ACCESS_RESOLVED_D.description: The rendering effect requires the depth buffer to be resolved if MSAA is enabled.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_MOTION_VECT.description: The rendering effect requires motion vectors to be produced.

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_ROUGHNESS.description: The rendering effect requires normals and roughness g-buffer to be produced (Forward+ only).

COMPOSITOR_EFFECT_FLAG_NEEDS_SEPARATE_SP.description: The rendering effect requires specular data to be separated out (Forward+ only).

DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

DECAL_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC.description: Linear filter for decals (use for non-pixel art decals). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look sharp but grainy. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

DECAL_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for decals (use for pixel art decals). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means decals at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

DECAL_TEXTURE_ALBEDO.description: Albedo texture slot in a decal (`Decal.texture_albedo`).

DECAL_TEXTURE_EMISSION.description: Emission texture slot in a decal (`Decal.texture_emission`).

DECAL_TEXTURE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `DecalTexture` enum.

DECAL_TEXTURE_NORMAL.description: Normal map texture slot in a decal (`Decal.texture_normal`).

DECAL_TEXTURE_ORM.description: Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic texture slot in a decal (`Decal.texture_orm`).

DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_HIGH.description: Highest quality DOF blur. Results in the smoothest looking blur by taking the most samples, but is also significantly slower.

DOF_BLUR_QUALITY_VERY_LOW.description: Lowest quality DOF blur. This is the fastest setting, but you may be able to see filtering artifacts.

DOF_BOKEH_BOX.description: Calculate the DOF blur using a box filter. The fastest option, but results in obvious lines in blur pattern.

DOF_BOKEH_CIRCLE.description: Calculates DOF blur using a circle shaped filter. Best quality and most realistic, but slowest. Use only for areas where a lot of performance can be dedicated to post-processing (e.g. cutscenes).

DOF_BOKEH_HEXAGON.description: Calculates DOF blur using a hexagon shaped filter.

ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_BG.description: Gather ambient light from whichever source is specified as the background.

ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR.description: Specify a specific `Color` for ambient light.

ENV_AMBIENT_SOURCE_SKY.description: Gather ambient light from the `Sky` regardless of what the background is.

ENV_BG_CAMERA_FEED.description: Displays a camera feed in the background.

ENV_BG_CANVAS.description: Use a specified canvas layer as the background. This can be useful for instantiating a 2D scene in a 3D world.

ENV_BG_CLEAR_COLOR.description: Use the clear color as background.

ENV_BG_COLOR.description: Use a specified color as the background.

ENV_BG_KEEP.description: Do not clear the background, use whatever was rendered last frame as the background.

ENV_BG_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `EnvironmentBG` enum.

ENV_BG_SKY.description: Use a sky resource for the background.

ENV_FOG_MODE_DEPTH.description: Use a simple fog model defined by start and end positions and a custom curve. While not physically accurate, this model can be useful when you need more artistic control.

ENV_FOG_MODE_EXPONENTIAL.description: Use a physically-based fog model defined primarily by fog density.

ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_ADDITIVE.description: Adds the glow effect to the scene.

ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_MIX.description: Mixes the glow image with the scene image. Best used with `Environment.glow_bloom` to avoid darkening the scene.

ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_REPLACE.description: Replaces all pixels' color by the glow effect. This can be used to simulate a full-screen blur effect by tweaking the glow parameters to match the original image's brightness or to preview glow configuration in the editor.

ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SCREEN.description: Adds the glow effect to the scene after modifying the glow influence based on the scene value; dark values will be highly influenced by glow and bright values will not be influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. `Environment.tonemap_white` is used to determine the maximum scene value where the glow should have no influence. When `Environment.tonemap_mode` is set to `Environment.TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR` and `Viewport.use_hdr_2d` is `true`, the parent window's `Window.get_output_max_linear_value` will be used as the maximum scene value.

ENV_GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SOFTLIGHT.description:
Adds the glow effect to the tonemapped image after modifying the glow influence based on the image value; dark values and bright values will not be influenced by glow and mid-range values will be highly influenced by glow. This approach avoids bright values becoming overly bright from the glow effect. The glow will have the largest influence on image values of `0.25` and will have no influence when applied to image values greater than `1.0`.

**Note:** This blend mode does not support HDR output because expects a maximum output value of `1.0`. It is recommended to use a different blend mode when rendering to an HDR screen.

ENV_REFLECTION_SOURCE_SKY.description: Use the `Sky` for reflections regardless of what the background is.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_10_FRAMES.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 10 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_15_FRAMES.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 15 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_20_FRAMES.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 20 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_25_FRAMES.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 25 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_30_FRAMES.description: Configure SDFGI to fully converge over 30 frames. This is the least responsive, but creates the least noisy result with a given ray count.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_IN_5_FRAMES.description: Converge SDFGI over 5 frames. This is the most responsive, but creates the most noisy result with a given ray count.

ENV_SDFGI_CONVERGE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `EnvironmentSDFGIFramesToConverge` enum.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_128.description: Throw 128 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has very high GPU requirements, but creates the least noisy result.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_16.description: Throw 16 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_32.description: Throw 32 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_4.description: Throw 4 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has the lowest GPU requirements, but creates the most noisy result.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_64.description: Throw 64 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_8.description: Throw 8 rays per frame when converging SDFGI.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_96.description: Throw 96 rays per frame when converging SDFGI. This has high GPU requirements.

ENV_SDFGI_RAY_COUNT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `EnvironmentSDFGIRayCount` enum.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_16_FRAMES.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 16 frames. This is the least responsive, but has the lowest GPU requirements.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_1_FRAME.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 1 frame. This is the most responsive, but has the highest GPU requirements.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_2_FRAMES.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 2 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_4_FRAMES.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 4 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_IN_8_FRAMES.description: Update indirect light from dynamic lights in SDFGI over 8 frames.

ENV_SDFGI_UPDATE_LIGHT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `EnvironmentSDFGIFramesToUpdateLight` enum.

ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_100_PERCENT.description: Use 100% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be as tall as they are wide. This is usually the best choice for highly vertical scenes. The downside is that light leaking may become more noticeable with thin floors and ceilings.

ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_50_PERCENT.description: Use 50% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. SDFGI cells will be twice as short as they are wide. This allows providing increased GI detail and reduced light leaking with thin floors and ceilings. This is usually the best choice for scenes that don't feature much verticality.

ENV_SDFGI_Y_SCALE_75_PERCENT.description: Use 75% scale for SDFGI on the Y (vertical) axis. This is a balance between the 50% and 100% SDFGI Y scales.

ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_ULTRA.description: Highest quality screen-space ambient occlusion. Uses the adaptive target setting which can be dynamically adjusted to smoothly balance performance and visual quality.

ENV_SSAO_QUALITY_VERY_LOW.description: Lowest quality of screen-space ambient occlusion.

ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_ULTRA.description: Highest quality screen-space indirect lighting. Uses the adaptive target setting which can be dynamically adjusted to smoothly balance performance and visual quality.

ENV_SSIL_QUALITY_VERY_LOW.description: Lowest quality of screen-space indirect lighting.

ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_DISABLED.description: Lowest quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections. Rough materials will not have blurrier screen-space reflections compared to smooth (non-rough) materials. This is the fastest option.

ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_HIGH.description: High quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections. This is the slowest option.

ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_LOW.description: Low quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections.

ENV_SSR_ROUGHNESS_QUALITY_MEDIUM.description: Medium quality of roughness filter for screen-space reflections.

ENV_TONE_MAPPER_ACES.description:
Uses a high-contrast film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Slightly slower than `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC`.

**Note:** This tonemapping operator is called "ACES Fitted" in Godot 3.x.

**Note:** This tonemapper does not support HDR output because it produces output in the SDR range. It is recommended to use a different tonemapper when rendering to an HDR screen.

ENV_TONE_MAPPER_AGX.description: Uses an adjustable film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Better than other tonemappers at maintaining the hue of colors as they become brighter. The slowest tonemapping option.

ENV_TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC.description:
Uses a film-like tonemapping curve to prevent clipping of bright values and provide better contrast than `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD`. Slightly slower than `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD`.

**Note:** This tonemapper does not support HDR output because it produces output in the SDR range. It is recommended to use a different tonemapper when rendering to an HDR screen.

ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR.description: Does not modify color data, resulting in a linear tonemapping curve which unnaturally clips bright values, causing bright lighting to look blown out. The simplest and fastest tonemapper.

ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD.description:
A simple tonemapping curve that rolls off bright values to prevent clipping. This results in an image that can appear dull and low contrast. Slower than `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR`.

**Note:** When `Environment.tonemap_white` is left at the default value of `1.0`, `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_REINHARD` produces an identical image to `ENV_TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR`.

FEATURE_MULTITHREADED.deprecated: This constant has not been used since Godot 3.0.

FEATURE_SHADERS.deprecated: This constant has not been used since Godot 3.0.

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_BOX.description: `FogVolume` will be shaped like a box.

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CONE.description: `FogVolume` will be shaped like a cone pointing upwards (in local coordinates). The cone's angle is set automatically to fill the size. The cone will be adjusted to fit within the size. Rotate the `FogVolume` node to reorient the cone. Non-uniform scaling via size is not supported (scale the `FogVolume` node instead).

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_CYLINDER.description: `FogVolume` will be shaped like an upright cylinder (in local coordinates). Rotate the `FogVolume` node to reorient the cylinder. The cylinder will be adjusted to fit within the size. Non-uniform scaling via size is not supported (scale the `FogVolume` node instead).

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_ELLIPSOID.description: `FogVolume` will be shaped like an ellipsoid (stretched sphere).

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `FogVolumeShape` enum.

FOG_VOLUME_SHAPE_WORLD.description: `FogVolume` will have no shape, will cover the whole world and will not be culled.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_BOOL.description: Boolean global shader parameter (`global uniform bool ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_BVEC2.description: 2-dimensional boolean vector global shader parameter (`global uniform bvec2 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_BVEC3.description: 3-dimensional boolean vector global shader parameter (`global uniform bvec3 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_BVEC4.description: 4-dimensional boolean vector global shader parameter (`global uniform bvec4 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_COLOR.description: Color global shader parameter (`global uniform vec4 ...`). Equivalent to `GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_VEC4` in shader code, but exposed as a `Color` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_FLOAT.description: Single-precision floating-point global shader parameter (`global uniform float ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_INT.description: Integer global shader parameter (`global uniform int ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_IVEC2.description: 2-dimensional integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform ivec2 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_IVEC3.description: 3-dimensional integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform ivec3 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_IVEC4.description: 4-dimensional integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform ivec4 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_MAT2.description: 2×2 matrix global shader parameter (`global uniform mat2 ...`). Exposed as a `PackedInt32Array` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_MAT3.description: 3×3 matrix global shader parameter (`global uniform mat3 ...`). Exposed as a `Basis` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_MAT4.description: 4×4 matrix global shader parameter (`global uniform mat4 ...`). Exposed as a `Projection` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `GlobalShaderParameterType` enum.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_RECT2.description: 2-dimensional floating-point rectangle global shader parameter (`global uniform vec4 ...`). Equivalent to `GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_VEC4` in shader code, but exposed as a `Rect2` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_RECT2I.description: 2-dimensional integer rectangle global shader parameter (`global uniform ivec4 ...`). Equivalent to `GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_IVEC4` in shader code, but exposed as a `Rect2i` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_SAMPLER2D.description: 2D sampler global shader parameter (`global uniform sampler2D ...`). Exposed as a `Texture2D` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_SAMPLER2DARRAY.description: 2D sampler array global shader parameter (`global uniform sampler2DArray ...`). Exposed as a `Texture2DArray` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_SAMPLER3D.description: 3D sampler global shader parameter (`global uniform sampler3D ...`). Exposed as a `Texture3D` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_SAMPLERCUBE.description: Cubemap sampler global shader parameter (`global uniform samplerCube ...`). Exposed as a `Cubemap` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_SAMPLEREXT.description: External sampler global shader parameter (`global uniform samplerExternalOES ...`). Exposed as an `ExternalTexture` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_TRANSFORM.description: 3-dimensional transform global shader parameter (`global uniform mat3x4 ...`). Exposed as a `Transform3D` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_TRANSFORM_2D.description: 2-dimensional transform global shader parameter (`global uniform mat2x3 ...`). Exposed as a `Transform2D` in the editor UI.

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_UINT.description: Unsigned integer global shader parameter (`global uniform uint ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_UVEC2.description: 2-dimensional unsigned integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform uvec2 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_UVEC3.description: 3-dimensional unsigned integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform uvec3 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_UVEC4.description: 4-dimensional unsigned integer vector global shader parameter (`global uniform uvec4 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_VEC2.description: 2-dimensional floating-point vector global shader parameter (`global uniform vec2 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_VEC3.description: 3-dimensional floating-point vector global shader parameter (`global uniform vec3 ...`).

GLOBAL_VAR_TYPE_VEC4.description: 4-dimensional floating-point vector global shader parameter (`global uniform vec4 ...`).

INSTANCE_FLAG_DRAW_NEXT_FRAME_IF_VISIBLE.description: When set, manually requests to draw geometry on next frame.

INSTANCE_FLAG_IGNORE_OCCLUSION_CULLING.description: Always draw, even if the instance would be culled by occlusion culling. Does not affect view frustum culling.

INSTANCE_FLAG_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `InstanceFlags` enum.

INSTANCE_FLAG_USE_BAKED_LIGHT.description: Allows the instance to be used in baked lighting.

INSTANCE_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_GI.description: Allows the instance to be used with dynamic global illumination.

INSTANCE_FOG_VOLUME.description: The instance is a fog volume.

INSTANCE_GEOMETRY_MASK.description: A combination of the flags of geometry instances (mesh, multimesh, immediate and particles).

INSTANCE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `InstanceType` enum.

INSTANCE_NONE.description: The instance does not have a type.

INSTANCE_OCCLUDER.description: The instance is an occlusion culling occluder.

INSTANCE_PARTICLES.description: The instance is a particle emitter.

INSTANCE_PARTICLES_COLLISION.description: The instance is a GPUParticles collision shape.

INSTANCE_REFLECTION_PROBE.description: The instance is a reflection probe.

INSTANCE_VISIBLITY_NOTIFIER.description: The instance is a visible on-screen notifier.

LIGHT_BAKE_DISABLED.description: Light is ignored when baking. This is the fastest mode, but the light will be taken into account when baking global illumination. This mode should generally be used for dynamic lights that change quickly, as the effect of global illumination is less noticeable on those lights.

LIGHT_BAKE_DYNAMIC.description: Light is taken into account in dynamic baking (`VoxelGI` and SDFGI (`Environment.sdfgi_enabled`) only). The light can be moved around or modified with global illumination updating in real-time. The light's global illumination appearance will be slightly different compared to `LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC`. This has a greater performance cost compared to `LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC`. When using SDFGI, the update speed of dynamic lights is affected by `ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/sdfgi/frames_to_update_lights`.

LIGHT_BAKE_STATIC.description: Light is taken into account in static baking (`VoxelGI`, `LightmapGI`, SDFGI (`Environment.sdfgi_enabled`)). The light can be moved around or modified, but its global illumination will not update in real-time. This is suitable for subtle changes (such as flickering torches), but generally not large changes such as toggling a light on and off.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL.description: Use orthogonal shadow projection for directional light.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_PARALLEL_2_SPLI.description: Use 2 splits for shadow projection when using directional light.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLI.description: Use 4 splits for shadow projection when using directional light.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_LIGHT_AND_SKY.description: Use DirectionalLight3D in both sky rendering and scene lighting.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY.description: Only use DirectionalLight3D in scene lighting.

LIGHT_DIRECTIONAL_SKY_MODE_SKY_ONLY.description: Only use DirectionalLight3D in sky rendering.

LIGHT_OMNI_SHADOW_CUBE.description: Use a cubemap shadow map for omni lights. Slower but better quality than dual paraboloid.

LIGHT_OMNI_SHADOW_DUAL_PARABOLOID.description: Use a dual paraboloid shadow map for omni lights.

LIGHT_PARAM_INDIRECT_ENERGY.description: The light's indirect energy multiplier (final indirect energy is `LIGHT_PARAM_ENERGY` \* `LIGHT_PARAM_INDIRECT_ENERGY`).

LIGHT_PARAM_INTENSITY.description: Constant representing the intensity of the light, measured in Lumens when dealing with a `SpotLight3D` or `OmniLight3D`, or measured in Lux with a `DirectionalLight3D`. Only used when `ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units` is `true`.

LIGHT_PARAM_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `LightParam` enum.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_BIAS.description: Bias for the shadow lookup to fix self-shadowing artifacts.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_BLUR.description: Blurs the edges of the shadow. Can be used to hide pixel artifacts in low resolution shadow maps. A high value can make shadows appear grainy and can cause other unwanted artifacts. Try to keep as near default as possible.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_FADE_START.description: Proportion of shadow max distance where the shadow will start to fade out.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_MAX_DISTANCE.description: The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_NORMAL_BIAS.description: Normal bias used to offset shadow lookup by object normal. Can be used to fix self-shadowing artifacts.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_OPACITY.description: The light's shadow opacity. Values lower than `1.0` make the light appear through shadows. This can be used to fake global illumination at a low performance cost.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_PANCAKE_SIZE.description: Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow. However, a high pancake size can cause artifacts in the shadows of large objects that are close to the edge of the frustum. Reducing the pancake size can help. Setting the size to `0` turns off the pancaking effect.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_1_OFFSET.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the first split.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_2_OFFSET.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the second split.

LIGHT_PARAM_SHADOW_SPLIT_3_OFFSET.description: Proportion of shadow atlas occupied by the third split. The fourth split occupies the rest.

LIGHT_PARAM_SIZE.description: The size of the light when using spot light or omni light. The angular size of the light when using directional light.

LIGHT_PARAM_VOLUMETRIC_FOG_ENERGY.description: The light's volumetric fog energy multiplier (final volumetric fog energy is `LIGHT_PARAM_ENERGY` \* `LIGHT_PARAM_VOLUMETRIC_FOG_ENERGY`).

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_LINEAR.description: Linear filter for light projectors (use for non-pixel art light projectors). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS.description: Linear filter for light projectors (use for non-pixel art light projectors). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_LINEAR_MIPMAPS_AN.description: Linear filter for light projectors (use for non-pixel art light projectors). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_NEAREST.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for light projectors (use for pixel art light projectors). No mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look sharp but grainy. This has roughly the same performance cost as using mipmaps.

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for light projectors (use for pixel art light projectors). Isotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look smooth but blurry. This has roughly the same performance cost as not using mipmaps.

LIGHT_PROJECTOR_FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAPS_A.description: Nearest-neighbor filter for light projectors (use for pixel art light projectors). Anisotropic mipmaps are used for rendering, which means light projectors at a distance will look smooth and sharp when viewed from oblique angles. This looks better compared to isotropic mipmaps, but is slower. The level of anisotropic filtering is defined by `ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`.

MATERIAL_RENDER_PRIORITY_MAX.description: The maximum renderpriority of all materials.

MATERIAL_RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN.description: The minimum renderpriority of all materials.

MAX_2D_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS.description: The maximum number of directional lights that can be rendered at a given time in 2D.

MAX_CURSORS.deprecated: This constant is not used by the engine.

MAX_GLOW_LEVELS.description: The maximum number of glow levels that can be used with the glow post-processing effect.

MAX_MESH_SURFACES.description: The maximum number of surfaces a mesh can have.

MULTIMESH_INTERP_QUALITY_FAST.description: MultiMesh physics interpolation favors speed over quality.

MULTIMESH_INTERP_QUALITY_HIGH.description: MultiMesh physics interpolation favors quality over speed.

NINE_PATCH_STRETCH.description: The nine patch gets stretched where needed.

NINE_PATCH_TILE.description: The nine patch gets filled with tiles where needed.

NINE_PATCH_TILE_FIT.description: The nine patch gets filled with tiles where needed and stretches them a bit if needed.

NO_INDEX_ARRAY.description: Marks an error that shows that the index array is empty.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_AXIS_X.description: Use the X axis for local billboarding.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_AXIS_Y.description: Use the Y axis for local billboarding.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_DISABLED.description: Do not read from CUSTOM when performing billboarding.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_W.description: Read from `CUSTOM.w` when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_X.description: Read from `CUSTOM.x` when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_Y.description: Read from `CUSTOM.y` when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

PARTICLES_ALIGN_CHANNEL_FILTER_Z.description: Read from `CUSTOM.z` when performing billboarding and use it as an angle, in radians.

PARTICLES_COLLISION_HEIGHTFIELD_RESOLUTI.description: Represents the size of the `ParticlesCollisionHeightfieldResolution` enum.

PARTICLES_COLLISION_TYPE_SDF_COLLIDE.description: Signed distance field collision type for `GPUParticles3D` (see `GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D`).

PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_INDEX.description: Draw particles in the order that they appear in the particles array.

PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_LIFETIME.description: Sort particles based on their lifetime. In other words, the particle with the highest lifetime is drawn at the front.

PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_REVERSE_LIFETIME.description: Sort particles based on the inverse of their lifetime. In other words, the particle with the lowest lifetime is drawn at the front.

PARTICLES_DRAW_ORDER_VIEW_DEPTH.description: Sort particles based on their distance to the camera.

PARTICLES_EMIT_FLAG_POSITION.description: Particle starts at the specified position.

PARTICLES_EMIT_FLAG_ROTATION_SCALE.description: Particle starts with specified rotation and scale.

PARTICLES_EMIT_FLAG_VELOCITY.description: Particle starts with the specified velocity vector, which defines the emission direction and speed.

PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_DISABLED.description: Do not align particle transforms relative to the camera or velocity.

PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_LOCAL_BILLBOAR.description: Billboard each particles around a local axis.

PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Y_TO_VELOCITY.description: Align each particle's Y axis to the velocity vector.

PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Z_BILLBOARD.description: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera.

PARTICLES_TRANSFORM_ALIGN_Z_BILLBOARD_Y_.description: Align each particle's Z axis to face the camera and Y axis to the velocity vector.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_CANVAS.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by the 2D canvas renderer.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_DRAW.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered while drawing the scene.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `PipelineSource` enum.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_MESH.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by loading a mesh.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_SPECIALIZATION.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered to optimize the current scene.

PIPELINE_SOURCE_SURFACE.description: Pipeline compilation that was triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene.

PRIMITIVE_LINES.description: Primitive to draw consists of lines.

PRIMITIVE_LINE_STRIP.description: Primitive to draw consists of a line strip from start to end.

PRIMITIVE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `PrimitiveType` enum.

PRIMITIVE_POINTS.description: Primitive to draw consists of points.

PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES.description: Primitive to draw consists of triangles.

PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP.description: Primitive to draw consists of a triangle strip (the last 3 vertices are always combined to make a triangle).

REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_COLOR.description: Apply custom ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size. See `reflection_probe_set_ambient_color` and `reflection_probe_set_ambient_energy`.

REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_DISABLED.description: Do not apply any ambient lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.

REFLECTION_PROBE_AMBIENT_ENVIRONMENT.description: Apply automatically-sourced environment lighting inside the reflection probe's box defined by its size.

REFLECTION_PROBE_UPDATE_ALWAYS.description: Reflection probe will update each frame. This mode is necessary to capture moving objects.

REFLECTION_PROBE_UPDATE_ONCE.description: Reflection probe will update reflections once and then stop.

RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED.description: Buffer memory used (in bytes). This includes vertex data, uniform buffers, and many miscellaneous buffer types used internally.

RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_CAN.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by the 2D canvas renderer.

RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_DRA.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered while drawing the scene. These compilations will show up as stutters during gameplay the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_MES.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by loading meshes. These compilations will show up as longer loading times the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SPE.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered to optimize the current scene. These compilations are done in the background and should not cause any stutters whatsoever.

RENDERING_INFO_PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SUR.description: Number of pipeline compilations that were triggered by building the surface cache before rendering the scene. These compilations will show up as a stutter when loading a scene the first time a user runs the game and the pipeline is required.

RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME.description: Number of draw calls performed to render in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME.description: Number of objects rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME.description: Number of points, lines, or triangles rendered in the current 3D scene. This varies depending on camera position and rotation.

RENDERING_INFO_VIDEO_MEM_USED.description: Video memory used (in bytes). When using the Forward+ or Mobile renderers, this is always greater than the sum of `RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED` and `RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED`, since there is miscellaneous data not accounted for by those two metrics. When using the Compatibility renderer, this is equal to the sum of `RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED` and `RENDERING_INFO_BUFFER_MEM_USED`.

SHADER_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ShaderMode` enum.

SHADER_PARTICLES.description: Shader is a particle shader (can be used in both 2D and 3D).

SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_DOUBLE_SIDED.description: Disable backface culling when rendering the shadow of the object. This is slightly slower but may result in more correct shadows.

SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_SHADOWS_ONLY.description: Only render the shadows from the object. The object itself will not be drawn.

SHADOW_QUALITY_HARD.description:
Lowest shadow filtering quality (fastest). Soft shadows are not available with this quality setting, which means the `Light3D.shadow_blur` property is ignored if `Light3D.light_size` and `Light3D.light_angular_distance` is `0.0`.

**Note:** The variable shadow blur performed by `Light3D.light_size` and `Light3D.light_angular_distance` is still effective when using hard shadow filtering. In this case, `Light3D.shadow_blur` *is* taken into account. However, the results will not be blurred, instead the blur amount is treated as a maximum radius for the penumbra.

SHADOW_QUALITY_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ShadowQuality` enum.

SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_HIGH.description: High low shadow filtering quality (slow). When using this quality setting, `Light3D.shadow_blur` is automatically multiplied by 1.5× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose `Light3D.light_size` or `Light3D.light_angular_distance` is `0.0`).

SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_ULTRA.description: Highest low shadow filtering quality (slowest). When using this quality setting, `Light3D.shadow_blur` is automatically multiplied by 2× to better make use of the high sample count. This increased blur also improves the stability of dynamic object shadows. This multiplier only applies to lights whose `Light3D.light_size` or `Light3D.light_angular_distance` is `0.0`).

SHADOW_QUALITY_SOFT_VERY_LOW.description: Very low shadow filtering quality (faster). When using this quality setting, `Light3D.shadow_blur` is automatically multiplied by 0.75× to avoid introducing too much noise. This division only applies to lights whose `Light3D.light_size` or `Light3D.light_angular_distance` is `0.0`).

SKY_MODE_AUTOMATIC.description: Automatically selects the appropriate process mode based on your sky shader. If your shader uses `TIME` or `POSITION`, this will use `SKY_MODE_REALTIME`. If your shader uses any of the `LIGHT_*` variables or any custom uniforms, this uses `SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL`. Otherwise, this defaults to `SKY_MODE_QUALITY`.

SKY_MODE_INCREMENTAL.description: Uses the same high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map as `SKY_MODE_QUALITY`, but updates over several frames. The number of frames is determined by `ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers`. Use this when you need highest quality radiance maps, but have a sky that updates slowly.

SKY_MODE_QUALITY.description: Uses high quality importance sampling to process the radiance map. In general, this results in much higher quality than `SKY_MODE_REALTIME` but takes much longer to generate. This should not be used if you plan on changing the sky at runtime. If you are finding that the reflection is not blurry enough and is showing sparkles or fireflies, try increasing `ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/ggx_samples`.

SKY_MODE_REALTIME.description:
Uses the fast filtering algorithm to process the radiance map. In general this results in lower quality, but substantially faster run times. If you need better quality, but still need to update the sky every frame, consider turning on `ProjectSettings.rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/fast_filter_high_quality`.

**Note:** The fast filtering algorithm is limited to 256×256 cubemaps, so `sky_set_radiance_size` must be set to `256`. Otherwise, a warning is printed and the overridden radiance size is ignored.

SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_COVER.description: Stretches the image to cover the entire screen while preserving aspect ratio.

SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_IGNORE.description: Stretches the image to cover the entire screen but doesn't preserve aspect ratio.

SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_KEEP.description: Stretches image to fullscreen while preserving aspect ratio.

SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_KEEP_HEIGHT.description: Stretches the width of the image based on the height of the screen.

SPLASH_STRETCH_MODE_KEEP_WIDTH.description: Stretches the height of the image based on the width of the screen.

SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_DISABLED.description: Disables subsurface scattering entirely, even on materials that have `BaseMaterial3D.subsurf_scatter_enabled` set to `true`. This has the lowest GPU requirements.

SUB_SURFACE_SCATTERING_QUALITY_HIGH.description: High subsurface scattering quality. This has the highest GPU requirements.

TEXTURE_DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBA8.description: OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.

TEXTURE_DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBA8_SRGB.description:
OpenGL texture format RGBA with four components, each with a bitdepth of 8.

When drawn to, an sRGB to linear color space conversion is performed.

TEXTURE_DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBAF.description: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA32F where there are four components, each a 32-bit floating-point value.

TEXTURE_DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBAH.description: OpenGL texture format GL_RGBA16F where there are four components, each a 16-bit "half-precision" floating-point value.

VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_4X.description: Use 4× anisotropic filtering. This is the default value.

VIEWPORT_ANISOTROPY_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `ViewportAnisotropicFiltering` enum.

VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ALWAYS.description: Always clear the viewport's render target before drawing.

VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER.description: Never clear the viewport's render target.

VIEWPORT_CLEAR_ONLY_NEXT_FRAME.description: Clear the viewport's render target on the next frame, then switch to `VIEWPORT_CLEAR_NEVER`.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_DECALS.description:
Draws the `Decal` cluster. Clustering determines where decals are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for decals.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_OMNI_LIGHTS.description:
Draws the `OmniLight3D` cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_REFLECTION_P.description:
Draws the `ReflectionProbe` cluster. Clustering determines where reflection probes are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for reflection probes.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_CLUSTER_SPOT_LIGHTS.description:
Draws the `SpotLight3D` cluster. Clustering determines where lights are positioned in screen-space, which allows the engine to only process these portions of the screen for lighting.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DECAL_ATLAS.description:
Draws the decal atlas that stores decal textures from `Decal`s.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DIRECTIONAL_SHADOW_A.description:
Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from `DirectionalLight3D`s in the upper left quadrant of the `Viewport`.

The slice of the camera frustum related to the shadow map cascade is superimposed to visualize coverage. The color of each slice matches the colors used for `VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS`. When shadow cascades are blended the overlap is taken into account when drawing the frustum slices.

The last cascade shows all frustum slices to illustrate the coverage of all slices.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLED.description: Debug draw is disabled. Default setting.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_DISABLE_LOD.description: Disable mesh LOD. All meshes are drawn with full detail, which can be used to compare performance.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_GI_BUFFER.description:
Draws the global illumination buffer from `VoxelGI` or SDFGI. Requires `VoxelGI` (at least one visible baked VoxelGI node) or SDFGI (`Environment.sdfgi_enabled`) to be enabled to have a visible effect.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_INTERNAL_BUFFER.description:
Internal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel output that will be used by post-processing effects.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_LIGHTING.description:
Objects are displayed with only light information.

**Note:** When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_MOTION_VECTORS.description:
Draws the motion vectors buffer. This is used by temporal antialiasing to correct for motion that occurs during gameplay.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_NORMAL_BUFFER.description: Normal buffer is drawn instead of regular scene so you can see the per-pixel normals that will be used by post-processing effects.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OCCLUDERS.description:
Draws the occlusion culling buffer. This low-resolution occlusion culling buffer is rasterized on the CPU and is used to check whether instances are occluded by other objects.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_OVERDRAW.description:
Objects are displayed semi-transparent with additive blending so you can see where they are drawing over top of one another. A higher overdraw (represented by brighter colors) means you are wasting performance on drawing pixels that are being hidden behind others.

**Note:** When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS.description:
Colors each PSSM split for the `DirectionalLight3D`s in the scene a different color so you can see where the splits are. In order (from closest to furthest from the camera), they are colored red, green, blue, and yellow.

**Note:** When using this debug draw mode, custom shaders are ignored since all materials in the scene temporarily use a debug material. This means the result from custom shader functions (such as vertex displacement) won't be visible anymore when using this debug draw mode.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SCENE_LUMINANCE.description:
Draws the estimated scene luminance. This is a 1×1 texture that is generated when autoexposure is enabled to control the scene's exposure.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ or Mobile rendering methods.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI.description:
Draws SDFGI cascade data. This is the data structure that is used to bounce lighting against and create reflections.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SDFGI_PROBES.description:
Draws SDFGI probe data. This is the data structure that is used to give indirect lighting dynamic objects moving within the scene.

When in the editor, left-clicking a probe will display additional bright dots that show its occlusion information. A white dot means the light is not occluded at all at the dot's position, while a red dot means the light is fully occluded. Intermediate values are possible.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SHADOW_ATLAS.description: Draws the shadow atlas that stores shadows from `OmniLight3D`s and `SpotLight3D`s in the upper left quadrant of the `Viewport`.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSAO.description:
Draws the screen space ambient occlusion texture instead of the scene so that you can clearly see how it is affecting objects. In order for this display mode to work, you must have `Environment.ssao_enabled` set in your `WorldEnvironment`.

**Note:** Only supported when using the Forward+ rendering method.

VIEWPORT_DEBUG_DRAW_SSIL.description:
