LOOP_NONE.description: The animation plays once and stops when it reaches the end, or the start if played in reverse.

LOOP_PINGPONG.description:
The animation alternates direction each time it reaches the end or start, playing forward and then in reverse repeatedly.

**Note:** Both `AnimatedSprite2D` and `AnimatedSprite3D` play the first/last frame for its duration only once at each end of the animation loop (instead of twice, once per forward/backward animation direction).

SpriteFrames.description: Sprite frame library for an `AnimatedSprite2D` or `AnimatedSprite3D` node. Contains frames and animation data for playback.

StandardMaterial3D.brief: A PBR (Physically Based Rendering) material to be used on 3D objects.
StandardMaterial3D.description: `StandardMaterial3D`'s properties are inherited from `BaseMaterial3D`. `StandardMaterial3D` uses separate textures for ambient occlusion, roughness and metallic maps. To use a single ORM map for all 3 textures, use an `ORMMaterial3D` instead.

StaticBody2D.brief: A 2D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
StaticBody2D.description:
A static 2D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform2D`.

When `StaticBody2D` is moved, it is teleported to its new position without affecting other physics bodies in its path. If this is not desired, use `AnimatableBody2D` instead.

`StaticBody2D` is useful for completely static objects like floors and walls, as well as moving surfaces like conveyor belts and circular revolving platforms (by using `constant_linear_velocity` and `constant_angular_velocity`).

constant_angular_velocity.description: The body's constant angular velocity. This does not rotate the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were rotating.

constant_linear_velocity.description: The body's constant linear velocity. This does not move the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were moving.

physics_material_override.description:
The physics material override for the body.

If a material is assigned to this property, it will be used instead of any other physics material, such as an inherited one.

StaticBody3D.brief: A 3D physics body that can't be moved by external forces. When moved manually, it doesn't affect other bodies in its path.
StaticBody3D.description:
A static 3D physics body. It can't be moved by external forces or contacts, but can be moved manually by other means such as code, `AnimationMixer`s (with `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_process` set to `AnimationMixer.ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`), and `RemoteTransform3D`.

When `StaticBody3D` is moved, it is teleported to its new position without affecting other physics bodies in its path. If this is not desired, use `AnimatableBody3D` instead.

`StaticBody3D` is useful for completely static objects like floors and walls, as well as moving surfaces like conveyor belts and circular revolving platforms (by using `constant_linear_velocity` and `constant_angular_velocity`).

constant_angular_velocity.description: The body's constant angular velocity. This does not rotate the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were rotating.

constant_linear_velocity.description: The body's constant linear velocity. This does not move the body, but affects touching bodies, as if it were moving.

physics_material_override.description:
The physics material override for the body.

If a material is assigned to this property, it will be used instead of any other physics material, such as an inherited one.

StatusIndicator.brief:
Application status indicator (aka notification area icon).

**Note:** Status indicator is implemented on macOS and Windows.

menu.description:
Status indicator native popup menu. If this is set, the `pressed` signal is not emitted.

**Note:** Native popup is only supported if `NativeMenu` supports `NativeMenu.FEATURE_POPUP_MENU` feature.

visible.description: If `true`, the status indicator is visible.

pressed.description: Emitted when the status indicator is pressed.

StreamPeer.brief: Abstract base class for interacting with streams.
StreamPeer.description:
StreamPeer is an abstract base class mostly used for stream-based protocols (such as TCP). It provides an API for sending and receiving data through streams as raw data or strings.

**Note:** When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the `INTERNET` permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

big_endian.description: If `true`, this `StreamPeer` will using big-endian format for encoding and decoding.

StreamPeerBuffer.brief: A stream peer used to handle binary data streams.
StreamPeerBuffer.description:
A data buffer stream peer that uses a byte array as the stream. This object can be used to handle binary data from network sessions. To handle binary data stored in files, `FileAccess` can be used directly.

A `StreamPeerBuffer` object keeps an internal cursor which is the offset in bytes to the start of the buffer. Get and put operations are performed at the cursor position and will move the cursor accordingly.

data_array.description: The underlying data buffer. Setting this value resets the cursor.

StreamPeerGZIP.brief: A stream peer that handles GZIP and deflate compression/decompression.
StreamPeerGZIP.description:
This class allows to compress or decompress data using GZIP/deflate in a streaming fashion. This is particularly useful when compressing or decompressing files that have to be sent through the network without needing to allocate them all in memory.

After starting the stream via `start_compression` (or `start_decompression`), calling `StreamPeer.put_partial_data` on this stream will compress (or decompress) the data, writing it to the internal buffer. Calling `StreamPeer.get_available_bytes` will return the pending bytes in the internal buffer, and `StreamPeer.get_partial_data` will retrieve the compressed (or decompressed) bytes from it. When the stream is over, you must call `finish` to ensure the internal buffer is properly flushed (make sure to call `StreamPeer.get_available_bytes` on last time to check if more data needs to be read after that).

StreamPeerSocket.brief: Abstract base class for interacting with socket streams.

STATUS_CONNECTED.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerSocket` that is connected to a host.

STATUS_CONNECTING.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerSocket` that is connecting to a host.

STATUS_ERROR.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerSocket` in error state.

STATUS_NONE.description: The initial status of the `StreamPeerSocket`. This is also the status after disconnecting.

StreamPeerSocket.description: StreamPeerSocket is an abstract base class that defines common behavior for socket-based streams.

StreamPeerTCP.brief: A stream peer that handles TCP connections.
StreamPeerTCP.description:
A stream peer that handles TCP connections. This object can be used to connect to TCP servers, or also is returned by a TCP server.

**Note:** When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the `INTERNET` permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

StreamPeerTLS.brief: A stream peer that handles TLS connections.

STATUS_CONNECTED.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerTLS` that is connected to a host.

STATUS_DISCONNECTED.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerTLS` that is disconnected.

STATUS_ERROR.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerTLS` in error state.

STATUS_ERROR_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH.description: An error status that shows a mismatch in the TLS certificate domain presented by the host and the domain requested for validation.

STATUS_HANDSHAKING.description: A status representing a `StreamPeerTLS` during handshaking.

StreamPeerTLS.description:
A stream peer that handles TLS connections. This object can be used to connect to a TLS server or accept a single TLS client connection.

**Note:** When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the `INTERNET` permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

StreamPeerUDS.brief: A stream peer that handles UNIX Domain Socket (UDS) connections.
StreamPeerUDS.description:
A stream peer that handles UNIX Domain Socket (UDS) connections. This object can be used to connect to UDS servers, or also is returned by a UDS server. Unix Domain Sockets provide inter-process communication on the same machine using the filesystem namespace.

**Note:** UNIX Domain Sockets are only available on UNIX-like systems (Linux, macOS, etc.) and are not supported on Windows.

StyleBox.brief: Abstract base class for defining stylized boxes for UI elements.
StyleBox.description:
`StyleBox` is an abstract base class for drawing stylized boxes for UI elements. It is used for panels, buttons, `LineEdit` backgrounds, `Tree` backgrounds, etc. and also for testing a transparency mask for pointer signals. If mask test fails on a `StyleBox` assigned as mask to a control, clicks and motion signals will go through it to the one below.

**Note:** For control nodes that have *Theme Properties*, the `focus` `StyleBox` is displayed over the `normal`, `hover` or `pressed` `StyleBox`. This makes the `focus` `StyleBox` more reusable across different nodes.

content_margin_bottom.description:
The bottom margin for the contents of this style box. Increasing this value reduces the space available to the contents from the bottom.

If this value is negative, it is ignored and a child-specific margin is used instead. For example, for `StyleBoxFlat`, the border thickness (if any) is used instead.

It is up to the code using this style box to decide what these contents are: for example, a `Button` respects this content margin for the textual contents of the button.

`get_margin` should be used to fetch this value as consumer instead of reading these properties directly. This is because it correctly respects negative values and the fallback mentioned above.

content_margin_left.description:
The left margin for the contents of this style box. Increasing this value reduces the space available to the contents from the left.

Refer to `content_margin_bottom` for extra considerations.

content_margin_right.description:
The right margin for the contents of this style box. Increasing this value reduces the space available to the contents from the right.

Refer to `content_margin_bottom` for extra considerations.

content_margin_top.description:
The top margin for the contents of this style box. Increasing this value reduces the space available to the contents from the top.

Refer to `content_margin_bottom` for extra considerations.

StyleBoxEmpty.description: An empty `StyleBox` that can be used to display nothing instead of the default style (e.g. it can "disable" `focus` styles).

StyleBoxFlat.brief: A customizable `StyleBox` that doesn't use a texture.
StyleBoxFlat.description:
By configuring various properties of this style box, you can achieve many common looks without the need of a texture. This includes optionally rounded borders, antialiasing, shadows, and skew.

Setting corner radius to high values is allowed. As soon as corners overlap, the stylebox will switch to a relative system:

```text
height = 30
corner_radius_top_left = 50
corner_radius_bottom_left = 100
```

The relative system now would take the 1:2 ratio of the two left corners to calculate the actual corner width. Both corners added will **never** be more than the height. Result:

```text
corner_radius_top_left: 10
corner_radius_bottom_left: 20
```

anti_aliasing.description:
Antialiasing draws a small ring around the edges, which fades to transparency. As a result, edges look much smoother. This is only noticeable when using rounded corners or `skew`.

**Note:** When using beveled corners with 45-degree angles (`corner_detail` = 1), it is recommended to set `anti_aliasing` to `false` to ensure crisp visuals and avoid possible visual glitches.

anti_aliasing_size.description:
This changes the size of the antialiasing effect. `1.0` is recommended for an optimal result at 100% scale, identical to how rounded rectangles are rendered in web browsers and most vector drawing software.

**Note:** Higher values may produce a blur effect but can also create undesired artifacts on small boxes with large-radius corners.

bg_color.description: The background color of the stylebox.

border_blend.description: If `true`, the border will fade into the background color.

border_color.description: Sets the color of the border.

border_width_bottom.description: Border width for the bottom border.

border_width_left.description: Border width for the left border.

border_width_right.description: Border width for the right border.

border_width_top.description: Border width for the top border.

corner_detail.description:
This sets the number of vertices used for each corner. Higher values result in rounder corners but take more processing power to compute. When choosing a value, you should take the corner radius (`set_corner_radius_all`) into account.

For corner radii less than 10, `4` or `5` should be enough. For corner radii less than 30, values between `8` and `12` should be enough.

A corner detail of `1` will result in chamfered corners instead of rounded corners, which is useful for some artistic effects.

corner_radius_bottom_left.description: The bottom-left corner's radius. If `0`, the corner is not rounded.

corner_radius_bottom_right.description: The bottom-right corner's radius. If `0`, the corner is not rounded.

corner_radius_top_left.description: The top-left corner's radius. If `0`, the corner is not rounded.

corner_radius_top_right.description: The top-right corner's radius. If `0`, the corner is not rounded.

draw_center.description: Toggles drawing of the inner part of the stylebox.

expand_margin_bottom.description:
Expands the stylebox outside of the control rect on the bottom edge. Useful in combination with `border_width_bottom` to draw a border outside the control rect.

**Note:** Unlike `StyleBox.content_margin_bottom`, `expand_margin_bottom` does *not* affect the size of the clickable area for `Control`s. This can negatively impact usability if used wrong, as the user may try to click an area of the StyleBox that cannot actually receive clicks.

expand_margin_left.description:
Expands the stylebox outside of the control rect on the left edge. Useful in combination with `border_width_left` to draw a border outside the control rect.

**Note:** Unlike `StyleBox.content_margin_left`, `expand_margin_left` does *not* affect the size of the clickable area for `Control`s. This can negatively impact usability if used wrong, as the user may try to click an area of the StyleBox that cannot actually receive clicks.

expand_margin_right.description:
Expands the stylebox outside of the control rect on the right edge. Useful in combination with `border_width_right` to draw a border outside the control rect.

**Note:** Unlike `StyleBox.content_margin_right`, `expand_margin_right` does *not* affect the size of the clickable area for `Control`s. This can negatively impact usability if used wrong, as the user may try to click an area of the StyleBox that cannot actually receive clicks.

expand_margin_top.description:
Expands the stylebox outside of the control rect on the top edge. Useful in combination with `border_width_top` to draw a border outside the control rect.

**Note:** Unlike `StyleBox.content_margin_top`, `expand_margin_top` does *not* affect the size of the clickable area for `Control`s. This can negatively impact usability if used wrong, as the user may try to click an area of the StyleBox that cannot actually receive clicks.

shadow_color.description: The color of the shadow. This has no effect if `shadow_size` is lower than 1.

shadow_offset.description: The shadow offset in pixels. Adjusts the position of the shadow relatively to the stylebox.

skew.description:
If set to a non-zero value on either axis, `skew` distorts the StyleBox horizontally and/or vertically. This can be used for "futuristic"-style UIs. Positive values skew the StyleBox towards the right (X axis) and upwards (Y axis), while negative values skew the StyleBox towards the left (X axis) and downwards (Y axis).

**Note:** To ensure text does not touch the StyleBox's edges, consider increasing the `StyleBox`'s content margin (see `StyleBox.content_margin_bottom`). It is preferable to increase the content margin instead of the expand margin (see `expand_margin_bottom`), as increasing the expand margin does not increase the size of the clickable area for `Control`s.

StyleBoxLine.brief: A `StyleBox` that displays a single line of a given color and thickness.
StyleBoxLine.description: A `StyleBox` that displays a single line of a given color and thickness. The line can be either horizontal or vertical. Useful for separators.

grow_begin.description: The number of pixels the line will extend before the `StyleBoxLine`'s bounds. If set to a negative value, the line will begin inside the `StyleBoxLine`'s bounds.

grow_end.description: The number of pixels the line will extend past the `StyleBoxLine`'s bounds. If set to a negative value, the line will end inside the `StyleBoxLine`'s bounds.

vertical.description: If `true`, the line will be vertical. If `false`, the line will be horizontal.

AXIS_STRETCH_MODE_STRETCH.description: Stretch the stylebox's texture. This results in visible distortion unless the texture size matches the stylebox's size perfectly.

AXIS_STRETCH_MODE_TILE.description: Repeats the stylebox's texture to match the stylebox's size according to the nine-patch system.

AXIS_STRETCH_MODE_TILE_FIT.description: Repeats the stylebox's texture to match the stylebox's size according to the nine-patch system. Unlike `AXIS_STRETCH_MODE_TILE`, the texture may be slightly stretched to make the nine-patch texture tile seamlessly.

StyleBoxTexture.description: A texture-based nine-patch `StyleBox`, in a way similar to `NinePatchRect`. This stylebox performs a 3×3 scaling of a texture, where only the center cell is fully stretched. This makes it possible to design bordered styles regardless of the stylebox's size.

axis_stretch_horizontal.description: Controls how the stylebox's texture will be stretched or tiled horizontally.

axis_stretch_vertical.description: Controls how the stylebox's texture will be stretched or tiled vertically.

draw_center.description: If `true`, the nine-patch texture's center tile will be drawn.

expand_margin_bottom.description: Expands the bottom margin of this style box when drawing, causing it to be drawn larger than requested.

expand_margin_left.description: Expands the left margin of this style box when drawing, causing it to be drawn larger than requested.

expand_margin_right.description: Expands the right margin of this style box when drawing, causing it to be drawn larger than requested.

expand_margin_top.description: Expands the top margin of this style box when drawing, causing it to be drawn larger than requested.

modulate_color.description: Modulates the color of the texture when this style box is drawn.

region_rect.description:
The region to use from the `texture`.

This is equivalent to first wrapping the `texture` in an `AtlasTexture` with the same region.

If empty (`Rect2(0, 0, 0, 0)`), the whole `texture` is used.

texture.description: The texture to use when drawing this style box.

texture_margin_bottom.description:
Increases the bottom margin of the 3×3 texture box.

A higher value means more of the source texture is considered to be part of the bottom border of the 3×3 box.

This is also the value used as fallback for `StyleBox.content_margin_bottom` if it is negative.

texture_margin_left.description:
Increases the left margin of the 3×3 texture box.

A higher value means more of the source texture is considered to be part of the left border of the 3×3 box.

This is also the value used as fallback for `StyleBox.content_margin_left` if it is negative.

texture_margin_right.description:
Increases the right margin of the 3×3 texture box.

A higher value means more of the source texture is considered to be part of the right border of the 3×3 box.

This is also the value used as fallback for `StyleBox.content_margin_right` if it is negative.

texture_margin_top.description:
Increases the top margin of the 3×3 texture box.

A higher value means more of the source texture is considered to be part of the top border of the 3×3 box.

This is also the value used as fallback for `StyleBox.content_margin_top` if it is negative.

SubViewport.brief: An interface to a game world that doesn't create a window or draw to the screen directly.

CLEAR_MODE_ALWAYS.description: Always clear the render target before drawing.

CLEAR_MODE_ONCE.description: Clear the render target on the next frame, then switch to `CLEAR_MODE_NEVER`.

UPDATE_DISABLED.description: Do not update the render target.

UPDATE_ONCE.description: Update the render target once, then switch to `UPDATE_DISABLED`.

UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE.description: Update the render target only when its parent is visible.

UPDATE_WHEN_VISIBLE.description: Update the render target only when it is visible. This is the default value.

SubViewport.description:
`SubViewport` Isolates a rectangular region of a scene to be displayed independently. This can be used, for example, to display UI in 3D space.

**Note:** `SubViewport` is a `Viewport` that isn't a `Window`, i.e. it doesn't draw anything by itself. To display anything, `SubViewport` must have a non-zero size and be either put inside a `SubViewportContainer` or assigned to a `ViewportTexture`.

**Note:** `InputEvent`s are not passed to a standalone `SubViewport` by default. To ensure `InputEvent` propagation, a `SubViewport` can be placed inside of a `SubViewportContainer`.

render_target_clear_mode.description:
The clear mode when the sub-viewport is used as a render target.

**Note:** This property is intended for 2D usage.

render_target_update_mode.description: The update mode when the sub-viewport is used as a render target.

size.description:
The width and height of the sub-viewport. Must be set to a value greater than or equal to 2 pixels on both dimensions. Otherwise, nothing will be displayed.

**Note:** If the parent node is a `SubViewportContainer` and its `SubViewportContainer.stretch` is `true`, the viewport size cannot be changed manually.

size_2d_override.description: The 2D size override of the sub-viewport. If either the width or height is `0`, the override is disabled.

size_2d_override_stretch.description: If `true`, the 2D size override affects stretch as well.

view_count.description: The number of view layers we are rendering to. Set this to `2` to enable stereo rendering.

SubViewportContainer.brief: A container used for displaying the contents of a `SubViewport`.
SubViewportContainer.description:
A container that displays the contents of underlying `SubViewport` child nodes. It uses the combined size of the `SubViewport`s as minimum size, unless `stretch` is enabled.

**Note:** Changing a `SubViewportContainer`'s `Control.scale` will cause its contents to appear distorted. To change its visual size without causing distortion, adjust the node's margins instead (if it's not already in a container).

**Note:** The `SubViewportContainer` forwards mouse-enter and mouse-exit notifications to its sub-viewports.

mouse_target.description:
Configure, if either the `SubViewportContainer` or alternatively the `Control` nodes of its `SubViewport` children should be available as targets of mouse-related functionalities, like identifying the drop target in drag-and-drop operations or cursor shape of hovered `Control` node.

If `false`, the `Control` nodes inside its `SubViewport` children are considered as targets.

If `true`, the `SubViewportContainer` itself will be considered as a target.

stretch.description:
If `true`, the sub-viewport will be automatically resized to the control's size.

**Note:** If `true`, this will prohibit changing `SubViewport.size` of its children manually.

stretch_shrink.description:
Divides the sub-viewport's effective resolution by this value while preserving its scale. This can be used to speed up rendering.

For example, a 1280×720 sub-viewport with `stretch_shrink` set to `2` will be rendered at 640×360 while occupying the same size in the container.

**Note:** `stretch` must be `true` for this property to work.

SubtweenTweener.description:
`SubtweenTweener` is used to execute a `Tween` as one step in a sequence defined by another `Tween`. See `Tween.tween_subtween` for more usage information.

**Note:** `Tween.tween_subtween` is the only correct way to create `SubtweenTweener`. Any `SubtweenTweener` created manually will not function correctly.

CUSTOM_MAX.description: Used to indicate a disabled custom channel.

CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM.description: Limits range of data passed to `set_custom` to signed normalized -1 to 1 stored in 8 bits per channel. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_SNORM`.

CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM.description: Limits range of data passed to `set_custom` to unsigned normalized 0 to 1 stored in 8 bits per channel. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA8_UNORM`.

CUSTOM_RGBA_FLOAT.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as full precision floats, and uses all color channels. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_FLOAT`.

CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as half precision floats and uses all color channels. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGBA_HALF`.

CUSTOM_RGB_FLOAT.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as full precision floats, and uses only red, green and blue color channels. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RGB_FLOAT`.

CUSTOM_RG_FLOAT.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as full precision floats, and uses only red and green color channels. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_FLOAT`.

CUSTOM_RG_HALF.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as half precision floats, and uses only red and green color channels. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_RG_HALF`.

CUSTOM_R_FLOAT.description: Stores data passed to `set_custom` as full precision floats, and uses only red color channel. See `Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM_R_FLOAT`.

SKIN_4_WEIGHTS.description: Each individual vertex can be influenced by only 4 bone weights.

SKIN_8_WEIGHTS.description: Each individual vertex can be influenced by up to 8 bone weights.

SyntaxHighlighter.brief: Base class for syntax highlighters. Provides syntax highlighting data to a `TextEdit`.
SyntaxHighlighter.description:
Base class for syntax highlighters. Provides syntax highlighting data to a `TextEdit`. The associated `TextEdit` will call into the `SyntaxHighlighter` on an as-needed basis.

**Note:** A `SyntaxHighlighter` instance should not be used across multiple `TextEdit` nodes.

SystemFont.brief: A font loaded from a system font. Falls back to a default theme font if not implemented on the host OS.
SystemFont.description:
`SystemFont` loads a font from a system font with the first matching name from `font_names`.

It will attempt to match font style, but it's not guaranteed.

The returned font might be part of a font collection or be a variable font with OpenType "weight", "width" and/or "italic" features set.

You can create `FontVariation` of the system font for precise control over its features.

**Note:** This class is implemented on iOS, Linux, macOS and Windows, on other platforms it will fallback to default theme font.

allow_system_fallback.description: If set to `true`, system fonts can be automatically used as fallbacks.

disable_embedded_bitmaps.description: If set to `true`, embedded font bitmap loading is disabled (bitmap-only and color fonts ignore this property).

font_italic.description: If set to `true`, italic or oblique font is preferred.

font_names.description: Array of font family names to search, first matching font found is used.

font_stretch.description: Preferred font stretch amount, compared to a normal width. A percentage value between `50%` and `200%`.

font_weight.description: Preferred weight (boldness) of the font. A value in the `100...999` range, normal font weight is `400`, bold font weight is `700`.

force_autohinter.description: If set to `true`, auto-hinting is supported and preferred over font built-in hinting.

generate_mipmaps.description: If set to `true`, generate mipmaps for the font textures.

keep_rounding_remainders.description: If set to `true`, when aligning glyphs to the pixel boundaries rounding remainders are accumulated to ensure more uniform glyph distribution. This setting has no effect if subpixel positioning is enabled.

modulate_color_glyphs.description: If set to `true`, color modulation is applied when drawing colored glyphs, otherwise it's applied to the monochrome glyphs only.

msdf_pixel_range.description: The width of the range around the shape between the minimum and maximum representable signed distance. If using font outlines, `msdf_pixel_range` must be set to at least *twice* the size of the largest font outline. The default `msdf_pixel_range` value of `16` allows outline sizes up to `8` to look correct.

msdf_size.description: Source font size used to generate MSDF textures. Higher values allow for more precision, but are slower to render and require more memory. Only increase this value if you notice a visible lack of precision in glyph rendering.

multichannel_signed_distance_field.description: If set to `true`, glyphs of all sizes are rendered using single multichannel signed distance field generated from the dynamic font vector data.

oversampling.description: If set to a positive value, overrides the oversampling factor of the viewport this font is used in. See `Viewport.oversampling`. This value doesn't override the `oversampling` parameter of `draw_*` methods.

subpixel_positioning.description: Font glyph subpixel positioning mode. Subpixel positioning provides shaper text and better kerning for smaller font sizes, at the cost of memory usage and font rasterization speed. Use `TextServer.SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_AUTO` to automatically enable it based on the font size.

TCPServer.description:
A TCP server. Listens to connections on a port and returns a `StreamPeerTCP` when it gets an incoming connection.

**Note:** When exporting to Android, make sure to enable the `INTERNET` permission in the Android export preset before exporting the project or using one-click deploy. Otherwise, network communication of any kind will be blocked by Android.

TLSOptions.brief: TLS configuration for clients and servers.
TLSOptions.description:
TLSOptions abstracts the configuration options for the `StreamPeerTLS` and `PacketPeerDTLS` classes.

Objects of this class cannot be instantiated directly, and one of the static methods `client`, `client_unsafe`, or `server` should be used instead.

TabBar.brief: A control that provides a horizontal bar with tabs.

ALIGNMENT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `AlignmentMode` enum.

CLOSE_BUTTON_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `CloseButtonDisplayPolicy` enum.

CLOSE_BUTTON_SHOW_ACTIVE_ONLY.description: Only show the close button on the currently active tab.

CLOSE_BUTTON_SHOW_ALWAYS.description: Show the close button on all tabs.

TabBar.description: A control that provides a horizontal bar with tabs. Similar to `TabContainer` but is only in charge of drawing tabs, not interacting with children.

clip_tabs.description: If `true`, tabs overflowing this node's width will be hidden, displaying two navigation buttons instead. Otherwise, this node's minimum size is updated so that all tabs are visible.

close_with_middle_mouse.description: If `true`, middle-clicking on a tab will emit the `tab_close_pressed` signal.

current_tab.description: The index of the current selected tab. A value of `-1` means that no tab is selected and can only be set when `deselect_enabled` is `true` or if all tabs are hidden or disabled.

deselect_enabled.description: If `true`, all tabs can be deselected so that no tab is selected. Click on the current tab to deselect it.

drag_to_rearrange_enabled.description: If `true`, tabs can be rearranged with mouse drag.

max_tab_width.description: Sets the maximum width which all tabs should be limited to. Unlimited if set to `0`.

scroll_to_selected.description: If `true`, the tab offset will be changed to keep the currently selected tab visible.

scrolling_enabled.description: if `true`, the mouse's scroll wheel can be used to navigate the scroll view.

select_with_rmb.description: If `true`, enables selecting a tab with the right mouse button.

switch_on_drag_hover.description: If `true`, hovering over a tab while dragging something will switch to that tab. Does not have effect when hovering another tab to rearrange. The delay for when this happens is dictated by `hover_switch_wait_msec`.

tab_alignment.description: The horizontal alignment of the tabs.

tab_close_display_policy.description: When the close button will appear on the tabs.

tab_count.description: The number of tabs currently in the bar.

tab_{index}/disabled.description:
If `true`, the tab at `index` is disabled.

**Note:** `index` is a value in the `0 .. tab_count - 1` range.

tab_{index}/icon.description:
If `true`, the tab at `index` is hidden.

**Note:** `index` is a value in the `0 .. tab_count - 1` range.

tab_{index}/title.description:
The title text of the tab at `index`.

**Note:** `index` is a value in the `0 .. tab_count - 1` range.

tab_{index}/tooltip.description:
The tooltip text of the tab at `index`.

**Note:** `index` is a value in the `0 .. tab_count - 1` range.

tabs_rearrange_group.description:
`TabBar`s with the same rearrange group ID will allow dragging the tabs between them. Enable drag with `drag_to_rearrange_enabled`.

Setting this to `-1` will disable rearranging between `TabBar`s.

active_tab_rearranged.description: Emitted when the active tab is rearranged via mouse drag. See `drag_to_rearrange_enabled`.

tab_button_pressed.description: Emitted when a tab's right button is pressed. See `set_tab_button_icon`.

tab_changed.description: Emitted when switching to another tab.

tab_clicked.description: Emitted when a tab is clicked, even if it is the current tab.

tab_close_pressed.description:
Emitted when a tab's close button is pressed or, if `close_with_middle_mouse` is `true`, when middle-clicking on a tab.

**Note:** Tabs are not removed automatically; this behavior needs to be coded manually. For example:

```csharp
GetNode<TabBar>("TabBar").TabClosePressed += GetNode<TabBar>("TabBar").RemoveTab;
```

tab_rmb_clicked.description: Emitted when a tab is right-clicked.

tab_selected.description: Emitted when a tab is selected via click, directional input, or script, even if it is the current tab.

button_highlight.description: Background of the tab and close buttons when they're being hovered with the cursor.

button_pressed.description: Background of the tab and close buttons when it's being pressed.

close.description: The icon for the close button (see `tab_close_display_policy`).

decrement.description: Icon for the left arrow button that appears when there are too many tabs to fit in the container width. When the button is disabled (i.e. the first tab is visible), it appears semi-transparent.

decrement_highlight.description: Icon for the left arrow button that appears when there are too many tabs to fit in the container width. Used when the button is being hovered with the cursor.

drop_mark.description: Icon shown to indicate where a dragged tab will be dropped (see `drag_to_rearrange_enabled`).

font.description: The font used to draw tab names.

font_hovered_color.description: Font color of the currently hovered tab. Does not apply to the selected tab.

font_outline_color.description: The tint of text outline of the tab name.

font_selected_color.description: Font color of the currently selected tab.

font_size.description: Font size of the tab names.

font_unselected_color.description: Font color of the other, unselected tabs.

h_separation.description: The horizontal separation between the elements inside tabs.

hover_switch_wait_msec.description: During a drag-and-drop, this is how many milliseconds to wait before switching the tab.

icon_hovered_color.description: Icon color of the currently hovered tab. Does not apply to the selected tab.

icon_max_width.description: The maximum allowed width of the tab's icon. This limit is applied on top of the default size of the icon, but before the value set with `set_tab_icon_max_width`. The height is adjusted according to the icon's ratio.

icon_selected_color.description: Icon color of the currently selected tab.

icon_unselected_color.description: Icon color of the other, unselected tabs.

increment_highlight.description: Icon for the right arrow button that appears when there are too many tabs to fit in the container width. Used when the button is being hovered with the cursor.

outline_size.description:

**Note:** If using a font with `FontFile.multichannel_signed_distance_field` enabled, its `FontFile.msdf_pixel_range` must be set to at least *twice* the value of `outline_size` for outline rendering to look correct. Otherwise, the outline may appear to be cut off earlier than intended.

The `tab_focus` `StyleBox` is displayed *over* the base `StyleBox` of the selected tab, so a partially transparent `StyleBox` should be used to ensure the base `StyleBox` remains visible. A `StyleBox` that represents an outline or an underline works well for this purpose. To disable the focus visual effect, assign a `StyleBoxEmpty` resource. Note that disabling the focus visual effect will harm keyboard/controller navigation usability, so this is not recommended for accessibility reasons.

**Note:** The drawing of the clickable tabs is handled by this node; `TabBar` is not needed.

current_tab.description:

A value of `-1` means that no tab is selected.

TextEdit.description:
A multiline text editor. It also has limited facilities for editing code, such as syntax highlighting support. For more advanced facilities for editing code, see `CodeEdit`.

While entering text, it is possible to insert special characters using Unicode, OEM or Windows alt codes:

- To enter Unicode codepoints, hold `Alt` and type the codepoint on the numpad. For example, to enter the character `á` (U+00E1), hold `Alt` and type `+E1` on the numpad (the leading zeroes can be omitted).

- To enter OEM codepoints, hold `Alt` and type the code on the numpad. For example, to enter the character `á` (OEM 160), hold `Alt` and type `160` on the numpad.

- To enter Windows codepoints, hold `Alt` and type the code on the numpad. For example, to enter the character `á` (Windows 0225), hold `Alt` and type `0`, `2`, `2`, `5` on the numpad. The leading zero here must **not** be omitted, as this is how Windows codepoints are distinguished from OEM codepoints.

**Note:** Most viewport, caret, and edit methods contain a `caret_index` argument for `caret_multiple` support. The argument should be one of the following: `-1` for all carets, `0` for the main caret, or greater than `0` for secondary carets in the order they were created.

**Note:** When holding down `Alt`, the vertical scroll wheel will scroll 5 times as fast as it would normally do. This also works in the Godot script editor.

autowrap_mode.description: If `wrap_mode` is set to `LINE_WRAPPING_BOUNDARY`, sets text wrapping mode.

backspace_deletes_composite_character_en.description: If `true` and `caret_mid_grapheme` is `false`, backspace deletes an entire composite character such as ❤️‍🩹, instead of deleting part of the composite character.

caret_blink_interval.description: The interval at which the caret blinks (in seconds).

caret_draw_when_editable_disabled.description: If `true`, caret will be visible when `editable` is disabled.

caret_mid_grapheme.description:
Allow moving caret, selecting and removing the individual composite character components.

**Note:** `Backspace` is always removing individual composite character components.

caret_move_on_right_click.description:
If `true`, a right-click moves the caret at the mouse position before displaying the context menu.

If `false`, the context menu ignores mouse location.

caret_multiple.description: If `true`, multiple carets are allowed. Left-clicking with `Alt` adds a new caret. See `add_caret` and `get_caret_count`.

caret_type.description: Set the type of caret to draw.

context_menu_enabled.description: If `true`, a right-click displays the context menu.

custom_word_separators.description: The characters to consider as word delimiters if `use_custom_word_separators` is `true`. The characters should be defined without separation, for example `#_!`.

deselect_on_focus_loss_enabled.description: If `true`, the selected text will be deselected when focus is lost.

drag_and_drop_selection_enabled.description: If `true`, allow drag and drop of selected text. Text can still be dropped from other sources.

draw_spaces.description: If `true`, the "space" character will have a visible representation.

draw_tabs.description: If `true`, the "tab" character will have a visible representation.

editable.description: If `false`, existing text cannot be modified and new text cannot be added.

emoji_menu_enabled.description: If `true`, "Emoji and Symbols" menu is enabled.

empty_selection_clipboard_enabled.description: If `true`, copying or cutting without a selection is performed on all lines with a caret. Otherwise, copy and cut require a selection.

highlight_all_occurrences.description: If `true`, all occurrences of the selected text will be highlighted.

highlight_current_line.description: If `true`, the line containing the cursor is highlighted.

indent_wrapped_lines.description: If `true`, all wrapped lines are indented to the same amount as the unwrapped line.

language.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

middle_mouse_paste_enabled.description:
If `false`, using middle mouse button to paste clipboard will be disabled.

**Note:** This method is only implemented on Linux.

minimap_draw.description: If `true`, a minimap is shown, providing an outline of your source code. The minimap uses a fixed-width text size.

minimap_width.description: The width, in pixels, of the minimap.

placeholder_text.description: Text shown when the `TextEdit` is empty. It is **not** the `TextEdit`'s default value (see `text`).

scroll_fit_content_height.description: If `true`, `TextEdit` fits its minimum height to the number of visible lines instead of scrolling vertically. If a maximum height is set (for example via `Control.custom_maximum_size`) and content exceeds it, a vertical scrollbar is shown.

scroll_fit_content_width.description: If `true`, `TextEdit` fits its minimum width to the widest line instead of scrolling horizontally. If a maximum width is set (for example via `Control.custom_maximum_size`) and content exceeds it, a horizontal scrollbar is shown.

scroll_horizontal.description: If there is a horizontal scrollbar, this determines the current horizontal scroll value in pixels.

scroll_past_end_of_file.description: Allow scrolling past the last line into "virtual" space.

scroll_smooth.description: Scroll smoothly over the text rather than jumping to the next location.

scroll_v_scroll_speed.description: Sets the scroll speed with the minimap or when `scroll_smooth` is enabled.

scroll_vertical.description: If there is a vertical scrollbar, this determines the current vertical scroll value in line numbers, starting at 0 for the top line.

selecting_enabled.description:
If `true`, text can be selected.

If `false`, text can not be selected by the user or by the `select` or `select_all` methods.

shortcut_keys_enabled.description: If `true`, shortcut keys for context menu items are enabled, even if the context menu is disabled.

structured_text_bidi_override.description: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.

structured_text_bidi_override_options.description: Set additional options for BiDi override.

syntax_highlighter.description:
The syntax highlighter to use.

**Note:** A `SyntaxHighlighter` instance should not be used across multiple `TextEdit` nodes.

tab_input_mode.description: If `true`, `ProjectSettings.input/ui_text_indent` input `Tab` character, otherwise it moves keyboard focus to the next `Control` in the scene.

use_custom_word_separators.description: If `false`, using `Ctrl + Left` or `Ctrl + Right` (`Cmd + Left` or `Cmd + Right` on macOS) bindings will use the behavior of `use_default_word_separators`. If `true`, it will also stop the caret if a character within `custom_word_separators` is detected. Useful for subword moving. This behavior also will be applied to the behavior of text selection.

use_default_word_separators.description: If `false`, using `Ctrl + Left` or `Ctrl + Right` (`Cmd + Left` or `Cmd + Right` on macOS) bindings will stop moving caret only if a space or punctuation is detected. If `true`, it will also stop the caret if a character is part of ``!"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^`{|}~``, the Unicode General Punctuation table, or the Unicode CJK Punctuation table. Useful for subword moving. This behavior also will be applied to the behavior of text selection.

virtual_keyboard_enabled.description: If `true`, the native virtual keyboard is enabled on platforms that support it.

virtual_keyboard_show_on_focus.description: If `true`, the native virtual keyboard is shown on focus events on platforms that support it.

wrap_mode.description: Sets the line wrapping mode to use.

caret_changed.description: Emitted when any caret changes position.

gutter_added.description: Emitted when a gutter is added.

gutter_clicked.description: Emitted when a gutter is clicked.

gutter_removed.description: Emitted when a gutter is removed.

lines_edited_from.description:
Emitted immediately when the text changes.

When text is added `from_line` will be less than `to_line`. On a remove `to_line` will be less than `from_line`.

text_set.description: Emitted when `clear` is called or `text` is set.

background_color.deprecated: Assign a `StyleBoxFlat` to `normal` instead, and set `StyleBoxFlat.bg_color` to the desired background color.

caret_background_color.description: `Color` of the text behind the caret when using a block caret.

caret_color.description: `Color` of the caret. This can be set to a fully transparent color to hide the caret entirely.

caret_width.description: The caret's width in pixels. Greater values can be used to improve accessibility by ensuring the caret is easily visible, or to ensure consistency with a large font size. If set to `0` or lower, the caret width is automatically set to 1 pixel and multiplied by the display scaling factor.

current_line_color.description: Background `Color` of the line containing the caret.

focus.description: Sets the `StyleBox` when in focus. The `focus` `StyleBox` is displayed *over* the base `StyleBox`, so a partially transparent `StyleBox` should be used to ensure the base `StyleBox` remains visible. A `StyleBox` that represents an outline or an underline works well for this purpose. To disable the focus visual effect, assign a `StyleBoxEmpty` resource. Note that disabling the focus visual effect will harm keyboard/controller navigation usability, so this is not recommended for accessibility reasons.

font_outline_color.description: The tint of text outline of the `TextEdit`.

font_readonly_color.description: Sets the font `Color` when `editable` is disabled.

font_selected_color.description: Sets the `Color` of the selected text. If equal to `Color(0, 0, 0, 0)`, it will be ignored.

line_spacing.description: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.

outline_size.description:
The size of the text outline.

**Note:** If using a font with `FontFile.multichannel_signed_distance_field` enabled, its `FontFile.msdf_pixel_range` must be set to at least *twice* the value of `outline_size` for outline rendering to look correct. Otherwise, the outline may appear to be cut off earlier than intended.

read_only.description: Sets the `StyleBox` of this `TextEdit` when `editable` is disabled.

search_result_border_color.description: `Color` of the border around text that matches the search query.

search_result_color.description: `Color` behind the text that matches the search query.

selection_color.description: Sets the highlight `Color` of text selections.

space.description: Sets a custom `Texture2D` for space text characters.

tab.description: Sets a custom `Texture2D` for tab text characters.

word_highlighted_color.description: Sets the highlight `Color` of multiple occurrences. `highlight_all_occurrences` has to be enabled.

wrap_offset.description: Sets an additional margin for line wrapping width.

TextLine.description: Abstraction over `TextServer` for handling a single line of text.

alignment.description: Sets text alignment within the line as if the line was horizontal.

ellipsis_char.description: Ellipsis character used for text clipping.

flags.description: Line alignment rules. For more info see `TextServer`.

preserve_control.description: If set to `true` text will display control characters.

preserve_invalid.description: If set to `true` text will display invalid characters.

text_overrun_behavior.description: The clipping behavior when the text exceeds the text line's set width.

TextMesh.description:
Generate a `PrimitiveMesh` from the text.

TextMesh can be generated only when using dynamic fonts with vector glyph contours. Bitmap fonts (including bitmap data in the TrueType/OpenType containers, like color emoji fonts) are not supported.

The UV layout is arranged in 4 horizontal strips, top to bottom: 40% of the height for the front face, 40% for the back face, 10% for the outer edges and 10% for the inner edges.

autowrap_mode.description: If set to something other than `TextServer.AUTOWRAP_OFF`, the text gets wrapped inside the node's bounding rectangle. If you resize the node, it will change its height automatically to show all the text.

curve_step.description:
Step (in pixels) used to approximate Bézier curves. Lower values result in smoother curves, but is slower to generate and render. Consider adjusting this according to the font size and the typical viewing distance.

**Note:** Changing this property will regenerate the mesh, which is a slow operation, especially with large font sizes and long texts.

depth.description: Depths of the mesh, if set to `0.0` only front surface, is generated, and UV layout is changed to use full texture for the front face only.

font.description: Font configuration used to display text.

font_size.description:
Font size of the `TextMesh`'s text. This property works in tandem with `pixel_size`. Higher values will result in a more detailed font, regardless of `curve_step` and `pixel_size`. Consider keeping this value below 63 (inclusive) for good performance, and adjust `pixel_size` as needed to enlarge text.

**Note:** Changing this property will regenerate the mesh, which is a slow operation, especially with large font sizes and long texts. To change the text's size in real-time efficiently, change the node's `Node3D.scale` instead.

horizontal_alignment.description: Controls the text's horizontal alignment. Supports left, center, right, and fill (also known as justify).

language.description: Language code used for line-breaking and text shaping algorithms. If left empty, the current locale is used instead.

line_spacing.description: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.

offset.description:
The text drawing offset (in pixels).

**Note:** Changing this property will regenerate the mesh, which is a slow operation. To change the text's position in real-time efficiently, change the node's `Node3D.position` instead.

pixel_size.description:
The size of one pixel's width on the text to scale it in 3D. This property works in tandem with `font_size`.

**Note:** Changing this property will regenerate the mesh, which is a slow operation, especially with large font sizes and long texts. To change the text's size in real-time efficiently, change the node's `Node3D.scale` instead.

structured_text_bidi_override.description: Set BiDi algorithm override for the structured text.

structured_text_bidi_override_options.description: Set additional options for BiDi override.

text.description:
The text to generate mesh from.

**Note:** Due to being a `Resource`, it doesn't follow the rules of `Node.auto_translate_mode`. If disabling translation is desired, it should be done manually with `Object.set_message_translation`.

uppercase.description: If `true`, all the text displays as UPPERCASE.

vertical_alignment.description: Controls the text's vertical alignment. Supports top, center, and bottom.

width.description: Text width (in pixels), used for fill alignment.

TextParagraph.description: Abstraction over `TextServer` for handling a single paragraph of text.

break_flags.description: Line breaking rules. For more info see `TextServer`.

custom_punctuation.description: Custom punctuation character list, used for word breaking. If set to empty string, server defaults are used.

ellipsis_char.description: Ellipsis character used for text clipping.

line_spacing.description: Additional vertical spacing between lines (in pixels), spacing is added to line descent. This value can be negative.

max_lines_visible.description: Limits the lines of text shown.

preserve_control.description: If set to `true` text will display control characters.

preserve_invalid.description: If set to `true` text will display invalid characters.

text_overrun_behavior.description: The clipping behavior when the text exceeds the paragraph's set width.

TextServer.brief: A server interface for font management and text rendering.

AUTOWRAP_ARBITRARY.description: Wraps the text inside the node's bounding rectangle by allowing to break lines at arbitrary positions, which is useful when very limited space is available.

AUTOWRAP_WORD.description: Wraps the text inside the node's bounding rectangle by soft-breaking between words.

AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART.description: Behaves similarly to `AUTOWRAP_WORD`, but force-breaks a word if that single word does not fit in one line.

BREAK_ADAPTIVE.description: Should be used only in conjunction with `BREAK_WORD_BOUND`, break the line between any unconnected graphemes, if it's impossible to break it between the words.

BREAK_GRAPHEME_BOUND.description: Break the line between any unconnected graphemes.

BREAK_MANDATORY.description: Break the line at the line mandatory break characters (e.g. `"\n"`).

BREAK_TRIM_EDGE_SPACES.description: Remove edge spaces from the broken line segments.

BREAK_TRIM_END_EDGE_SPACES.description:
Remove spaces and line break characters from the end of broken line segments.

E.g, after line breaking, the first segment of the following text `test  \n  next`, is `test` if the flag is set, and `test  \n` if it is not.

BREAK_TRIM_INDENT.description: Subtract first line indentation width from all lines after the first one.

BREAK_TRIM_START_EDGE_SPACES.description:
Remove spaces and line break characters from the start of broken line segments.

E.g, after line breaking, the second segment of the following text `test  \n  next`, is `next` if the flag is set, and `next` if it is not.

BREAK_WORD_BOUND.description: Break the line between the words.

CONTOUR_CURVE_TAG_OFF_CONIC.description: Contour point isn't on the curve, but serves as a control point for a conic (quadratic) Bézier arc.

CONTOUR_CURVE_TAG_OFF_CUBIC.description: Contour point isn't on the curve, but serves as a control point for a cubic Bézier arc.

CONTOUR_CURVE_TAG_ON.description: Contour point is on the curve.

DIRECTION_AUTO.description: Text direction is determined based on contents and current locale.

DIRECTION_INHERITED.description: Text writing direction is the same as base string writing direction. Used for BiDi override only.

DIRECTION_LTR.description: Text is written from left to right.

DIRECTION_RTL.description: Text is written from right to left.

FEATURE_BREAK_ITERATORS.description: TextServer supports complex line/word breaking rules (e.g. dictionary based).

FEATURE_CONTEXT_SENSITIVE_CASE_CONVERSIO.description: TextServer supports locale dependent and context sensitive case conversion.

FEATURE_FONT_DYNAMIC.description: TextServer supports loading dynamic (TrueType, OpeType, etc.) fonts.

FEATURE_FONT_MSDF.description: TextServer supports multichannel signed distance field dynamic font rendering.

FEATURE_UNICODE_IDENTIFIERS.description: TextServer supports UAX #31 identifier validation, see `is_valid_identifier`.

FEATURE_UNICODE_SECURITY.description: TextServer supports [Unicode Technical Report #36](https://unicode.org/reports/tr36/) and [Unicode Technical Standard #39](https://unicode.org/reports/tr39/) based spoof detection features.

FEATURE_USE_SUPPORT_DATA.description: TextServer require external data file for some features, see `load_support_data`.

FIXED_SIZE_SCALE_ENABLED.description: Bitmap font is scaled to an arbitrary (fractional) size. This is the recommended option for non-pixel art fonts.

FIXED_SIZE_SCALE_INTEGER_ONLY.description: Bitmap font is scaled to the closest integer multiple of the font's fixed size. This is the recommended option for pixel art fonts.

FONT_ANTIALIASING_GRAY.description: Font glyphs are rasterized as 8-bit grayscale anti-aliased bitmaps.

FONT_ANTIALIASING_LCD.description:
Font glyphs are rasterized for LCD screens.

LCD subpixel layout is determined by the value of the `ProjectSettings.gui/theme/lcd_subpixel_layout` setting.

LCD subpixel anti-aliasing mode is suitable only for rendering horizontal, unscaled text in 2D.

FONT_ANTIALIASING_NONE.description: Font glyphs are rasterized as 1-bit bitmaps.

FONT_FIXED_WIDTH.description: Font has fixed-width characters (also known as monospace).

FONT_LCD_SUBPIXEL_LAYOUT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `FontLCDSubpixelLayout` enum.

FONT_LCD_SUBPIXEL_LAYOUT_NONE.description: Unknown or unsupported subpixel layout, LCD subpixel antialiasing is disabled.

GRAPHEME_IS_BREAK_SOFT.description: Grapheme is optional break point (e.g. space).

GRAPHEME_IS_CONNECTED.description: Grapheme is connected to the previous grapheme. Breaking line before this grapheme is not safe.

GRAPHEME_IS_EMBEDDED_OBJECT.description: Grapheme is an object replacement character for the embedded object.

GRAPHEME_IS_RTL.description: Grapheme is part of right-to-left or bottom-to-top run.

GRAPHEME_IS_SAFE_TO_INSERT_TATWEEL.description: It is safe to insert a U+0640 before this grapheme for elongation.

GRAPHEME_IS_VALID.description: Grapheme is supported by the font, and can be drawn.

GRAPHEME_IS_VIRTUAL.description: Grapheme is not part of source text, it was added by justification process.

HINTING_LIGHT.description: Use the light font hinting mode.

HINTING_NONE.description: Disables font hinting (smoother but less crisp).

HINTING_NORMAL.description:
Use the default font hinting mode (crisper but less smooth).

**Note:** This hinting mode changes both horizontal and vertical glyph metrics. If applied to monospace font, some glyphs might have different width.

JUSTIFICATION_AFTER_LAST_TAB.description: Only apply justification to the part of the text after the last tab.

JUSTIFICATION_CONSTRAIN_ELLIPSIS.description: Apply justification to the trimmed line with ellipsis.

JUSTIFICATION_DO_NOT_SKIP_SINGLE_LINE.description: Always apply justification to the paragraphs with a single line (`JUSTIFICATION_SKIP_LAST_LINE` and `JUSTIFICATION_SKIP_LAST_LINE_WITH_VISIBLE_CHARS` are ignored).

JUSTIFICATION_KASHIDA.description: Justify text by adding and removing kashidas.

JUSTIFICATION_SKIP_LAST_LINE.description: Do not apply justification to the last line of the paragraph.

JUSTIFICATION_SKIP_LAST_LINE_WITH_VISIBL.description: Do not apply justification to the last line of the paragraph with visible characters (takes precedence over `JUSTIFICATION_SKIP_LAST_LINE`).

JUSTIFICATION_TRIM_EDGE_SPACES.description: Remove trailing and leading spaces from the justified text.

JUSTIFICATION_WORD_BOUND.description: Justify text by changing width of the spaces between the words.

ORIENTATION_VERTICAL.description:
Left to right text is written vertically from top to bottom.

Right to left text is written vertically from bottom to top.

OVERRUN_ADD_ELLIPSIS.description: Determines whether an ellipsis should be added at the end of the text.

OVERRUN_ENFORCE_ELLIPSIS.description: Determines whether the ellipsis at the end of the text is enforced and may not be hidden.

OVERRUN_JUSTIFICATION_AWARE.description: Accounts for the text being justified before attempting to trim it (see `JustificationFlag`).

OVERRUN_SHORT_STRING_ELLIPSIS.description: Determines whether the ellipsis should be added regardless of the string length, otherwise it is added only if the string is 6 characters or longer.

OVERRUN_TRIM.description: Trims the text when it exceeds the given width.

OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS.description: Trims the text per character and adds an ellipsis to indicate that parts are hidden if trimmed text is 6 characters or longer.

OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS_FORCE.description: Trims the text per character and adds an ellipsis to indicate that parts are hidden regardless of trimmed text length.

OVERRUN_TRIM_WORD_ELLIPSIS.description: Trims the text per word and adds an ellipsis to indicate that parts are hidden if trimmed text is 6 characters or longer.

OVERRUN_TRIM_WORD_ELLIPSIS_FORCE.description: Trims the text per word and adds an ellipsis to indicate that parts are hidden regardless of trimmed text length.

OVERRUN_TRIM_WORD_ONLY.description: Trims the text per word instead of per grapheme.

SPACING_BOTTOM.description: Spacing at the bottom of the line.

SPACING_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `SpacingType` enum.

SPACING_TOP.description: Spacing at the top of the line.

STRUCTURED_TEXT_CUSTOM.description: User defined structured text BiDi override function.

STRUCTURED_TEXT_LIST.description: BiDi override for lists. Structured text options: list separator `String`.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_AUTO.description:
Glyph horizontal position is rounded based on font size.

- To one quarter of the pixel size if font size is smaller or equal to `SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_QUARTER_MAX_SIZE`.

- To one half of the pixel size if font size is smaller or equal to `SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_HALF_MAX_SIZE`.

- To the whole pixel size for larger fonts.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_DISABLED.description: Glyph horizontal position is rounded to the whole pixel size, each glyph is rasterized once.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_HALF.description: Glyph horizontal position is rounded to one half of the pixel size, each glyph is rasterized up to two times.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_HALF_MAX_SIZE.description: Maximum font size which will use "one half of the pixel" subpixel positioning in `SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_AUTO` mode.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_QUARTER.description: Glyph horizontal position is rounded to one quarter of the pixel size, each glyph is rasterized up to four times.

SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_ONE_QUARTER_MAX_SIZ.description: Maximum font size which will use "one quarter of the pixel" subpixel positioning in `SUBPIXEL_POSITIONING_AUTO` mode.

VC_CHARS_AFTER_SHAPING.description: Displays glyphs that are mapped to the first `Label.visible_characters` or `RichTextLabel.visible_characters` characters from the beginning of the text.

VC_CHARS_BEFORE_SHAPING.description:
Trims text before the shaping. e.g, increasing `Label.visible_characters` or `RichTextLabel.visible_characters` value is visually identical to typing the text.

**Note:** In this mode, trimmed text is not processed at all. It is not accounted for in line breaking and size calculations.

VC_GLYPHS_AUTO.description: Displays `Label.visible_ratio` or `RichTextLabel.visible_ratio` glyphs, starting from the left or from the right, depending on `Control.layout_direction` value.

VC_GLYPHS_LTR.description: Displays `Label.visible_ratio` or `RichTextLabel.visible_ratio` glyphs, starting from the left.

VC_GLYPHS_RTL.description: Displays `Label.visible_ratio` or `RichTextLabel.visible_ratio` glyphs, starting from the right.

TextServer.description:
`TextServer` is the API backend for managing fonts and rendering text.

**Note:** This is a low-level API, consider using `TextLine`, `TextParagraph`, and `Font` classes instead.

This is an abstract class, so to get the currently active `TextServer` instance, use the following code:

```csharp
var ts = TextServerManager.GetPrimaryInterface();
```

TextServerAdvanced.brief: An advanced text server with support for BiDi, complex text layout, and contextual OpenType features. Used in Godot by default.
TextServerAdvanced.description: An implementation of `TextServer` that uses HarfBuzz, ICU and SIL Graphite to support BiDi, complex text layouts and contextual OpenType features. This is Godot's default primary `TextServer` interface.

TextServerDummy.brief: A dummy text server that can't render text or manage fonts.

TextServerExtension.description: External `TextServer` implementations should inherit from this class.

TextServerManager.description:
`TextServerManager` is the API backend for loading, enumerating, and switching `TextServer`s.

**Note:** Switching text server at runtime is possible, but will invalidate all fonts and text buffers. Make sure to unload all controls, fonts, and themes before doing so.

interface_added.description: Emitted when a new interface has been added.

interface_removed.description: Emitted when an interface is removed.

Texture.brief: Base class for all texture types.
Texture.description: `Texture` is the base class for all texture types. Common texture types are `Texture2D` and `ImageTexture`. See also `Image`.

Texture2D.description:
A texture works by registering an image in the video hardware, which then can be used in 3D models or 2D `Sprite2D` or GUI `Control`.

Textures are often created by loading them from a file. See `@GDScript.load`.

`Texture2D` is a base for other resources. It cannot be used directly.

**Note:** The maximum texture size is 16384×16384 pixels due to graphics hardware limitations. Larger textures may fail to import.

Texture2DArray.brief: A single texture resource which consists of multiple, separate images. Each image has the same dimensions and number of mipmap levels.
Texture2DArray.description:
A Texture2DArray is different from a Texture3D: The Texture2DArray does not support trilinear interpolation between the `Image`s, i.e. no blending. See also `Cubemap` and `CubemapArray`, which are texture arrays with specialized cubemap functions.

A Texture2DArray is also different from an `AtlasTexture`: In a Texture2DArray, all images are treated separately. In an atlas, the regions (i.e. the single images) can be of different sizes. Furthermore, you usually need to add a padding around the regions, to prevent accidental UV mapping to more than one region. The same goes for mipmapping: Mipmap chains are handled separately for each layer. In an atlas, the slicing has to be done manually in the fragment shader.

To create such a texture file yourself, reimport your image files using the Godot Editor import presets. To create a Texture2DArray from code, use `ImageTextureLayered.create_from_images` on an instance of the Texture2DArray class.

Texture2DArrayRD.brief: Texture Array for 2D that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
Texture2DArrayRD.description:
This texture array class allows you to use a 2D array texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc.

**Note:** `Texture2DArrayRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `Texture2DArray` instead.

Texture2DRD.brief: Texture for 2D that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
Texture2DRD.description:
This texture class allows you to use a 2D texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc.

**Note:** `Texture2DRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `Texture2D` instead.

texture_rd_rid.description: The RID of the texture object created on the `RenderingDevice`.

Texture3D.description:
Base class for `ImageTexture3D` and `CompressedTexture3D`. Cannot be used directly, but contains all the functions necessary for accessing the derived resource types. `Texture3D` is the base class for all 3-dimensional texture types. See also `TextureLayered`.

All images need to have the same width, height and number of mipmap levels.

To create such a texture file yourself, reimport your image files using the Godot Editor import presets.

Texture3DRD.brief: Texture for 3D that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
Texture3DRD.description:
This texture class allows you to use a 3D texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc.

**Note:** `Texture3DRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `Texture3D` instead.

texture_rd_rid.description: The RID of the texture object created on the `RenderingDevice`.

TextureButton.brief: Texture-based button. Supports Pressed, Hover, Disabled and Focused states.

STRETCH_KEEP.description: The texture keeps its original size and stays in the bounding rectangle's top-left corner.

STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT.description: Scale the texture to fit the node's bounding rectangle, but maintain the texture's aspect ratio.

STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED.description: Scale the texture to fit the node's bounding rectangle, center it, and maintain its aspect ratio.

STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_COVERED.description: Scale the texture so that the shorter side fits the bounding rectangle. The other side clips to the node's limits.

STRETCH_KEEP_CENTERED.description: The texture keeps its original size and stays centered in the node's bounding rectangle.

STRETCH_SCALE.description: Scale to fit the node's bounding rectangle.

STRETCH_TILE.description: Tile inside the node's bounding rectangle.

TextureButton.description:
`TextureButton` has the same functionality as `Button`, except it uses sprites instead of Godot's `Theme` resource. It is faster to create, but it doesn't support localization like more complex `Control`s.

See also `BaseButton` which contains common properties and methods associated with this node.

**Note:** Setting a texture for the "normal" state (`texture_normal`) is recommended. If `texture_normal` is not set, the `TextureButton` will still receive input events and be clickable, but the user will not be able to see it unless they activate another one of its states with a texture assigned (e.g., hover over it to show `texture_hover`).

ignore_texture_size.description: If `true`, the size of the texture won't be considered for minimum size calculation, so the `TextureButton` can be shrunk down past the texture size.

stretch_mode.description: Controls the texture's behavior when you resize the node's bounding rectangle. See the `StretchMode` constants for available options.

texture_click_mask.description: Pure black and white `BitMap` image to use for click detection. On the mask, white pixels represent the button's clickable area. Use it to create buttons with curved shapes.

texture_disabled.description: Texture to display when the node is disabled. See `BaseButton.disabled`. If not assigned, the `TextureButton` displays `texture_normal` instead.

texture_focused.description: Texture to *overlay on the base texture* when the node has mouse or keyboard focus. Because `texture_focused` is displayed on top of the base texture, a partially transparent texture should be used to ensure the base texture remains visible. A texture that represents an outline or an underline works well for this purpose. To disable the focus visual effect, assign a fully transparent texture of any size. Note that disabling the focus visual effect will harm keyboard/controller navigation usability, so this is not recommended for accessibility reasons.

texture_hover.description: Texture to display when the mouse hovers over the node. If not assigned, the `TextureButton` displays `texture_normal` instead when hovered over.

texture_normal.description: Texture to display by default, when the node is **not** in the disabled, hover or pressed state. This texture is still displayed in the focused state, with `texture_focused` drawn on top.

texture_pressed.description: Texture to display on mouse down over the node, if the node has keyboard focus and the player presses the Enter key or if the player presses the `BaseButton.shortcut` key. If not assigned, the `TextureButton` displays `texture_hover` instead when pressed.

TextureCubemapArrayRD.brief: Texture Array for Cubemaps that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
TextureCubemapArrayRD.description:
This texture class allows you to use a cubemap array texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc.

**Note:** `TextureCubemapArrayRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `CubemapArray` instead.

TextureCubemapRD.brief: Texture for Cubemap that is bound to a texture created on the `RenderingDevice`.
TextureCubemapRD.description:
This texture class allows you to use a cubemap texture created directly on the `RenderingDevice` as a texture for materials, meshes, etc.

**Note:** `TextureCubemapRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `Cubemap` instead.

TextureLayered.brief: Base class for texture types which contain the data of multiple `Image`s. Each image is of the same size and format.

LAYERED_TYPE_CUBEMAP.description: Texture is a `Cubemap`, with each side in its own layer (6 in total).

LAYERED_TYPE_CUBEMAP_ARRAY.description: Texture is a `CubemapArray`, with each cubemap being made of 6 layers.

TextureLayered.description:
Base class for `ImageTextureLayered` and `CompressedTextureLayered`. Cannot be used directly, but contains all the functions necessary for accessing the derived resource types. See also `Texture3D`.

Data is set on a per-layer basis. For `Texture2DArray`s, the layer specifies the array layer.

All images need to have the same width, height and number of mipmap levels.

A `TextureLayered` can be loaded with `ResourceLoader.load`.

Internally, Godot maps these files to their respective counterparts in the target rendering driver (Vulkan, OpenGL3).

TextureLayeredRD.brief: Abstract base class for layered texture RD types.
TextureLayeredRD.description:
Base class for `Texture2DArrayRD`, `TextureCubemapRD` and `TextureCubemapArrayRD`. Cannot be used directly, but contains all the functions necessary for accessing the derived resource types.

**Note:** `TextureLayeredRD` is intended for low-level usage with `RenderingDevice`. For most use cases, use `TextureLayered` instead.

texture_rd_rid.description: The RID of the texture object created on the `RenderingDevice`.

TextureProgressBar.brief: Texture-based progress bar. Useful for loading screens and life or stamina bars.

FILL_BILINEAR_LEFT_AND_RIGHT.description: The `texture_progress` fills from the center, expanding both towards the left and the right.

FILL_BILINEAR_TOP_AND_BOTTOM.description: The `texture_progress` fills from the center, expanding both towards the top and the bottom.

FILL_BOTTOM_TO_TOP.description: The `texture_progress` fills from bottom to top.

FILL_CLOCKWISE.description: Turns the node into a radial bar. The `texture_progress` fills clockwise. See `radial_center_offset`, `radial_initial_angle` and `radial_fill_degrees` to control the way the bar fills up.

FILL_CLOCKWISE_AND_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE.description: Turns the node into a radial bar. The `texture_progress` fills radially from the center, expanding both clockwise and counterclockwise. See `radial_center_offset`, `radial_initial_angle` and `radial_fill_degrees` to control the way the bar fills up.

FILL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE.description: Turns the node into a radial bar. The `texture_progress` fills counterclockwise. See `radial_center_offset`, `radial_initial_angle` and `radial_fill_degrees` to control the way the bar fills up.

FILL_LEFT_TO_RIGHT.description: The `texture_progress` fills from left to right.

FILL_RIGHT_TO_LEFT.description: The `texture_progress` fills from right to left.

FILL_TOP_TO_BOTTOM.description: The `texture_progress` fills from top to bottom.

TextureProgressBar.description: TextureProgressBar works like `ProgressBar`, but uses up to 3 textures instead of Godot's `Theme` resource. It can be used to create horizontal, vertical and radial progress bars.

fill_mode.description: The fill direction. See `FillMode` for possible values.

nine_patch_stretch.description: If `true`, Godot treats the bar's textures like in `NinePatchRect`. Use the `stretch_margin_*` properties like `stretch_margin_bottom` to set up the nine patch's 3×3 grid. When using a radial `fill_mode`, this setting will only enable stretching for `texture_progress`, while `texture_under` and `texture_over` will be treated like in `NinePatchRect`.

radial_center_offset.description:
Offsets `texture_progress` if `fill_mode` is `FILL_CLOCKWISE`, `FILL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`, or `FILL_CLOCKWISE_AND_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`.

**Note:** The effective radial center always stays within the `texture_progress` bounds. If you need to move it outside the texture's bounds, modify the `texture_progress` to contain additional empty space where needed.

radial_fill_degrees.description:
Upper limit for the fill of `texture_progress` if `fill_mode` is `FILL_CLOCKWISE`, `FILL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`, or `FILL_CLOCKWISE_AND_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`. When the node's `value` is equal to its `max_value`, the texture fills up to this angle.

See `Range.value`, `Range.max_value`.

radial_initial_angle.description:
Starting angle for the fill of `texture_progress` if `fill_mode` is `FILL_CLOCKWISE`, `FILL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`, or `FILL_CLOCKWISE_AND_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`. When the node's `value` is equal to its `min_value`, the texture doesn't show up at all. When the `value` increases, the texture fills and tends towards `radial_fill_degrees`.

**Note:** `radial_initial_angle` is wrapped between `0` and `360` degrees (inclusive).

stretch_margin_bottom.description: The height of the 9-patch's bottom row. A margin of 16 means the 9-slice's bottom corners and side will have a height of 16 pixels. You can set all 4 margin values individually to create panels with non-uniform borders. Only effective if `nine_patch_stretch` is `true`.

stretch_margin_left.description: The width of the 9-patch's left column. Only effective if `nine_patch_stretch` is `true`.

stretch_margin_right.description: The width of the 9-patch's right column. Only effective if `nine_patch_stretch` is `true`.
