This occurs when HDR output is enabled or disabled and when any HDR output luminance values of the window have changed, such as when the player adjusts their screen brightness setting or moves the window to a different screen. `output_max_linear_value` is the new value.

theme_changed.description: Emitted when the `NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED` notification is sent.

title_changed.description: Emitted when window title bar text is changed.

titlebar_changed.description: Emitted when window title bar decorations are changed, e.g. macOS window enter/exit full screen mode, or extend-to-title flag is changed.

visibility_changed.description: Emitted when `Window` is made visible or disappears.

window_input.description: Emitted when the `Window` is currently focused and receives any input, passing the received event as an argument. The event's position, if present, is in the embedder's coordinate system.

close.description: The icon for the close button.

close_h_offset.description: Horizontal position offset of the close button, relative to the end of the title bar, towards the beginning of the title bar.

close_pressed.description: The icon for the close button when it's being pressed.

close_v_offset.description: Vertical position offset of the close button, relative to the bottom of the title bar, towards the top of the title bar.

embedded_border.description:
The background style used when the `Window` is embedded. Note that this is drawn only under the window's content, excluding the title. For proper borders and title bar style, you can use `expand_margin_*` properties of `StyleBoxFlat`.

**Note:** The content background will not be visible unless `transparent` is enabled.

embedded_unfocused_border.description: The background style used when the `Window` is embedded and unfocused.

resize_margin.description: Defines the outside margin at which the window border can be grabbed with mouse and resized.

title_color.description: The color of the title's text.

title_font.description: The font used to draw the title.

title_font_size.description: The size of the title font.

title_outline_modulate.description: The color of the title's text outline.

title_outline_size.description: The size of the title outline.

WorkerThreadPool.brief: A singleton that allocates some `Thread`s on startup, used to offload tasks to these threads.

World2D.brief: A resource that holds all components of a 2D world, such as a canvas and a physics space.
World2D.description: Class that has everything pertaining to a 2D world: A physics space, a canvas, and a sound space. 2D nodes register their resources into the current 2D world.

canvas.description: The `RID` of this world's canvas resource. Used by the `RenderingServer` for 2D drawing.

direct_space_state.description: Direct access to the world's physics 2D space state. Used for querying current and potential collisions. When using multi-threaded physics, access is limited to `Node._physics_process` in the main thread.

navigation_map.description: The `RID` of this world's navigation map. Used by the `NavigationServer2D`.

space.description: The `RID` of this world's physics space resource. Used by the `PhysicsServer2D` for 2D physics, treating it as both a space and an area.

World3D.brief: A resource that holds all components of a 3D world, such as a visual scenario and a physics space.
World3D.description: Class that has everything pertaining to a world: A physics space, a visual scenario, and a sound space. 3D nodes register their resources into the current 3D world.

camera_attributes.description: The default `CameraAttributes` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.

direct_space_state.description: Direct access to the world's physics 3D space state. Used for querying current and potential collisions. When using multi-threaded physics, access is limited to `Node._physics_process` in the main thread.

fallback_environment.description: The World3D's fallback environment will be used if `environment` fails or is missing.

navigation_map.description: The `RID` of this world's navigation map. Used by the `NavigationServer3D`.

WorldBoundaryShape2D.brief: A 2D world boundary (half-plane) shape used for physics collision.
WorldBoundaryShape2D.description: A 2D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics. `WorldBoundaryShape2D` works like an infinite straight line that forces all physics bodies to stay above it. The line's normal determines which direction is considered as "above" and in the editor, the smaller line over it represents this direction. It can for example be used for endless flat floors.

distance.description:
The distance from the origin to the line, expressed in terms of `normal` (according to its direction and magnitude). Actual absolute distance from the origin to the line can be calculated as `abs(distance) / normal.length()`.

In the scalar equation of the line `ax + by = d`, this is `d`, while the `(a, b)` coordinates are represented by the `normal` property.

normal.description: The line's normal, typically a unit vector. Its direction indicates the non-colliding half-plane. Can be of any length but zero. Defaults to `Vector2.UP`.

WorldBoundaryShape3D.brief: A 3D world boundary (half-space) shape used for physics collision.
WorldBoundaryShape3D.description:
A 3D world boundary shape, intended for use in physics. `WorldBoundaryShape3D` works like an infinite plane that forces all physics bodies to stay above it. The `plane`'s normal determines which direction is considered as "above" and in the editor, the line over the plane represents this direction. It can for example be used for endless flat floors.

**Note:** When the physics engine is set to **Jolt Physics** in the project settings (`ProjectSettings.physics/3d/physics_engine`), `WorldBoundaryShape3D` has a finite size (centered at the shape's origin). It can be adjusted by changing `ProjectSettings.physics/jolt_physics_3d/limits/world_boundary_shape_size`.

plane.description: The `Plane` used by the `WorldBoundaryShape3D` for collision.

WorldEnvironment.brief: Default environment properties for the entire scene (post-processing effects, lighting and background settings).
WorldEnvironment.description:
The `WorldEnvironment` node is used to configure the default `Environment` for the scene.

The parameters defined in the `WorldEnvironment` can be overridden by an `Environment` node set on the current `Camera3D`. Additionally, only one `WorldEnvironment` may be instantiated in a given scene at a time.

The `WorldEnvironment` allows the user to specify default lighting parameters (e.g. ambient lighting), various post-processing effects (e.g. SSAO, DOF, Tonemapping), and how to draw the background (e.g. solid color, skybox). Usually, these are added in order to improve the realism/color balance of the scene.

camera_attributes.description: The default `CameraAttributes` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.

compositor.description: The default `Compositor` resource to use if none set on the `Camera3D`.

environment.description: The `Environment` resource used by this `WorldEnvironment`, defining the default properties.

X509Certificate.description:
The X509Certificate class represents an X509 certificate. Certificates can be loaded and saved like any other `Resource`.

They can be used as the server certificate in `StreamPeerTLS.accept_stream` (along with the proper `CryptoKey`), and to specify the only certificate that should be accepted when connecting to a TLS server via `StreamPeerTLS.connect_to_stream`.

XMLParser.brief: Provides a low-level interface for creating parsers for XML files.

NODE_CDATA.description: A node type for CDATA (Character Data) sections, e.g. `<![CDATA[CDATA section]]>`.

NODE_COMMENT.description: A comment node type, e.g. `<!--A comment-->`.

NODE_ELEMENT.description: An element node type, also known as a tag, e.g. `<title>`.

NODE_ELEMENT_END.description: An end of element node type, e.g. `</title>`.

NODE_NONE.description: There's no node (no file or buffer opened).

NODE_TEXT.description: A text node type, i.e. text that is not inside an element. This includes whitespace.

XRAnchor3D.brief: An anchor point in AR space.
XRAnchor3D.description:
The `XRAnchor3D` point is an `XRNode3D` that maps a real world location identified by the AR platform to a position within the game world. For example, as long as plane detection in ARKit is on, ARKit will identify and update the position of planes (tables, floors, etc.) and create anchors for them.

This node is mapped to one of the anchors through its unique ID. When you receive a signal that a new anchor is available, you should add this node to your scene for that anchor. You can predefine nodes and set the ID; the nodes will simply remain on `(0, 0, 0)` until a plane is recognized.

Keep in mind that, as long as plane detection is enabled, the size, placing and orientation of an anchor will be updated as the detection logic learns more about the real world out there especially if only part of the surface is in view.

XRBodyModifier3D.brief: A node for driving body meshes from `XRBodyTracker` data.

BODY_UPDATE_HANDS.description: The skeleton's hand joints are updated.

BODY_UPDATE_LOWER_BODY.description: The skeleton's lower body joints are updated.

BODY_UPDATE_UPPER_BODY.description: The skeleton's upper body joints are updated.

BONE_UPDATE_FULL.description: The skeleton's bones are fully updated (both position and rotation) to match the tracked bones.

BONE_UPDATE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `BoneUpdate` enum.

BONE_UPDATE_ROTATION_ONLY.description: The skeleton's bones are only rotated to align with the tracked bones, preserving bone length.

XRBodyModifier3D.description:
This node uses body tracking data from an `XRBodyTracker` to pose the skeleton of a body mesh.

Positioning of the body is performed by creating an `XRNode3D` ancestor of the body mesh driven by the same `XRBodyTracker`.

The body tracking position-data is scaled by `Skeleton3D.motion_scale` when applied to the skeleton, which can be used to adjust the tracked body to match the scale of the body model.

body_tracker.description: The name of the `XRBodyTracker` registered with `XRServer` to obtain the body tracking data from.

body_update.description: Specifies the body parts to update.

bone_update.description: Specifies the type of updates to perform on the bones.

JOINT_FLAG_ORIENTATION_TRACKED.description: The joint's orientation is actively tracked. May not be set if tracking has been temporarily lost.

JOINT_FLAG_ORIENTATION_VALID.description: The joint's orientation data is valid.

JOINT_FLAG_POSITION_TRACKED.description: The joint's position is actively tracked. May not be set if tracking has been temporarily lost.

JOINT_FLAG_POSITION_VALID.description: The joint's position data is valid.

JOINT_LEFT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Left index finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERMED.description: Left index finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_LEFT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMAL.description: Left index finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Left middle finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERME.description: Left middle finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_LEFT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMA.description: Left middle finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Left pinky finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERMED.description: Left pinky finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_LEFT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMAL.description: Left pinky finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Left ring finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_LEFT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERMEDI.description: Left ring finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_LEFT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMAL.description: Left ring finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `Joint` enum.

JOINT_RIGHT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Right index finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERME.description: Right index finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_INDEX_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMA.description: Right index finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Right middle finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERM.description: Right middle finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_MIDDLE_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIM.description: Right middle finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Right pinky finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERME.description: Right pinky finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_PINKY_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMA.description: Right pinky finger phalanx proximal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_DISTAL.description: Right ring finger phalanx distal joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_INTERMED.description: Right ring finger phalanx intermediate joint.

JOINT_RIGHT_RING_FINGER_PHALANX_PROXIMAL.description: Right ring finger phalanx proximal joint.

XRBodyTracker.description:
A body tracking system will create an instance of this object and add it to the `XRServer`. This tracking system will then obtain skeleton data, convert it to the Godot Humanoid skeleton and store this data on the `XRBodyTracker` object.

Use `XRBodyModifier3D` to animate a body mesh using body tracking data.

body_flags.description: The type of body tracking data captured.

has_tracking_data.description: If `true`, the body tracking data is valid.

XRCamera3D.brief: A camera node which automatically positions itself based on XR tracking data.
XRCamera3D.description:
A camera node which automatically positions itself based on XR tracking data.

In contrast to `XRController3D`, the render thread has access to more up-to-date tracking data, and the location of the `XRCamera3D` node can lag a few milliseconds behind what is used for rendering.

**Note:** If `Viewport.use_xr` is `true`, most of the camera properties are overridden by the active `XRInterface`. The only properties that can be trusted are the near and far planes.

XRController3D.brief: A 3D node representing a spatially-tracked controller.
XRController3D.description:
This is a helper 3D node that is linked to the tracking of controllers. It also offers several handy passthroughs to the state of buttons and such on the controllers.

Controllers are linked by their ID. You can create controller nodes before the controllers are available. If your game always uses two controllers (one for each hand), you can predefine the controllers with ID 1 and 2; they will become active as soon as the controllers are identified. If you expect additional controllers to be used, you should react to the signals and add XRController3D nodes to your scene.

The position of the controller node is automatically updated by the `XRServer`. This makes this node ideal to add child nodes to visualize the controller.

The current `XRInterface` defines the names of inputs. In the case of OpenXR, these are the names of actions in the current action set from the OpenXR action map.

button_pressed.description: Emitted when a button on this controller is pressed.

button_released.description: Emitted when a button on this controller is released.

input_float_changed.description: Emitted when a trigger or similar input on this controller changes value.

input_vector2_changed.description: Emitted when a thumbstick or thumbpad on this controller is moved.

profile_changed.description: Emitted when the interaction profile on this controller is changed.

XRControllerTracker.description:
An instance of this object represents a controller that is tracked.

As controllers are turned on and the `XRInterface` detects them, instances of this object are automatically added to this list of active tracking objects accessible through the `XRServer`.

The `XRController3D` consumes objects of this type and should be used in your project.

XRFaceModifier3D.brief: A node for driving standard face meshes from `XRFaceTracker` weights.
XRFaceModifier3D.description:
This node applies weights from an `XRFaceTracker` to a mesh with supporting face blend shapes.

The [Unified Expressions](https://docs.vrcft.io/docs/tutorial-avatars/tutorial-avatars-extras/unified-blendshapes) blend shapes are supported, as well as ARKit and SRanipal blend shapes.

The node attempts to identify blend shapes based on name matching. Blend shapes should match the names listed in the [Unified Expressions Compatibility](https://docs.vrcft.io/docs/tutorial-avatars/tutorial-avatars-extras/compatibility/overview) chart.

FT_BROW_DOWN.description: Pulls both eyebrows down and in.

FT_BROW_DOWN_LEFT.description: Pulls the left eyebrow down and in.

FT_BROW_DOWN_RIGHT.description: Pulls the right eyebrow down and in.

FT_CHEEK_SUCK_LEFT.description: Sucks in the left side cheek.

FT_CHEEK_SUCK_RIGHT.description: Sucks in the right side cheek.

FT_EYE_SQUINT_LEFT.description: Squeezes the left eye socket muscles.

FT_EYE_SQUINT_RIGHT.description: Squeezes the right eye socket muscles.

FT_LIP_FUNNEL_LOWER_LEFT.description: Lower left lip part pushes into a funnel.

FT_LIP_FUNNEL_LOWER_RIGHT.description: Lower right lip part pushes into a funnel.

FT_LIP_FUNNEL_UPPER_LEFT.description: Upper left lip part pushes into a funnel.

FT_LIP_FUNNEL_UPPER_RIGHT.description: Upper right lip part pushes into a funnel.

FT_LIP_PUCKER_LOWER_LEFT.description: Lower left lip part pushes outwards.

FT_LIP_PUCKER_LOWER_RIGHT.description: Lower right lip part pushes outwards.

FT_LIP_PUCKER_UPPER_LEFT.description: Upper left lip part pushes outwards.

FT_LIP_PUCKER_UPPER_RIGHT.description: Upper right lip part pushes outwards.

FT_LIP_SUCK_CORNER_LEFT.description: Left lip corner folds into the mouth.

FT_LIP_SUCK_CORNER_RIGHT.description: Right lip corner folds into the mouth.

FT_LIP_SUCK_LOWER_LEFT.description: Lower left lip part tucks in the mouth.

FT_LIP_SUCK_LOWER_RIGHT.description: Lower right lip part tucks in the mouth.

FT_LIP_SUCK_UPPER_LEFT.description: Upper left lip part tucks in the mouth.

FT_LIP_SUCK_UPPER_RIGHT.description: Upper right lip part tucks in the mouth.

FT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `BlendShapeEntry` enum.

FT_MOUTH_CORNER_PULL_LEFT.description: Left lip corner pulls diagonally up and out.

FT_MOUTH_CORNER_PULL_RIGHT.description: Right lip corner pulls diagonally up and out.

FT_MOUTH_DIMPLE_LEFT.description: Left lip corner is pushed backwards.

FT_MOUTH_DIMPLE_RIGHT.description: Right lip corner is pushed backwards.

FT_MOUTH_LOWER_DOWN_LEFT.description: Lower left part of the lip pulls up.

FT_MOUTH_LOWER_DOWN_RIGHT.description: Lower right part of the lip pulls up.

FT_MOUTH_PRESS_LEFT.description: Left side lips press and flatten together vertically.

FT_MOUTH_PRESS_RIGHT.description: Right side lips press and flatten together vertically.

FT_MOUTH_RAISER_LOWER.description: Raises and slightly pushes out the lower mouth.

FT_MOUTH_RAISER_UPPER.description: Raises and slightly pushes out the upper mouth.

FT_MOUTH_SAD_LEFT.description: Left side of the mouth expresses sadness.

FT_MOUTH_SAD_RIGHT.description: Right side of the mouth expresses sadness.

FT_MOUTH_SMILE_LEFT.description: Left side of the mouth smiles.

FT_MOUTH_SMILE_RIGHT.description: Right side of the mouth smiles.

FT_MOUTH_STRETCH_LEFT.description: Mouth corner lip pulls out and down.

FT_MOUTH_STRETCH_RIGHT.description: Mouth corner lip pulls out and down.

FT_MOUTH_TIGHTENER_LEFT.description: Left side lips squeeze together horizontally.

FT_MOUTH_TIGHTENER_RIGHT.description: Right side lips squeeze together horizontally.

FT_MOUTH_UPPER_DEEPEN_LEFT.description: Upper left lip part pushes in the cheek.

FT_MOUTH_UPPER_DEEPEN_RIGHT.description: Upper right lip part pushes in the cheek.

FT_MOUTH_UPPER_UP_LEFT.description: Upper left part of the lip pulls up.

FT_MOUTH_UPPER_UP_RIGHT.description: Upper right part of the lip pulls up.

FT_TONGUE_BLEND_DOWN.description: Tongue arches up then down inside the mouth.

FT_TONGUE_CURL_UP.description: Tongue arches down then up inside the mouth.

FT_TONGUE_OUT.description: Tongue visibly sticks out of the mouth.

FT_TONGUE_ROLL.description: Sides of the tongue funnel, creating a roll.

FT_TONGUE_TWIST_LEFT.description: Tongue tip rotates counter-clockwise, with the rest following gradually.

FT_TONGUE_TWIST_RIGHT.description: Tongue tip rotates clockwise, with the rest following gradually.

XRFaceTracker.description:
An instance of this object represents a tracked face and its corresponding blend shapes. The blend shapes come from the [Unified Expressions](https://docs.vrcft.io/docs/tutorial-avatars/tutorial-avatars-extras/unified-blendshapes) standard, and contain extended details and visuals for each blend shape. Additionally the [Tracking Standard Comparison](https://docs.vrcft.io/docs/tutorial-avatars/tutorial-avatars-extras/compatibility/overview) page documents the relationship between Unified Expressions and other standards.

As face trackers are turned on they are registered with the `XRServer`.

blend_shapes.description: The array of face blend shape weights with indices corresponding to the `BlendShapeEntry` enum.

XRHandModifier3D.brief: A node for driving hand meshes from `XRHandTracker` data.

BONE_UPDATE_FULL.description: The skeleton's bones are fully updated (both position and rotation) to match the tracked bones.

BONE_UPDATE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `BoneUpdate` enum.

BONE_UPDATE_ROTATION_ONLY.description: The skeleton's bones are only rotated to align with the tracked bones, preserving bone length.

XRHandModifier3D.description:
This node uses hand tracking data from an `XRHandTracker` to pose the skeleton of a hand mesh.

Positioning of hands is performed by creating an `XRNode3D` ancestor of the hand mesh driven by the same `XRHandTracker`.

The hand tracking position-data is scaled by `Skeleton3D.motion_scale` when applied to the skeleton, which can be used to adjust the tracked hand to match the scale of the hand model.

bone_update.description: Specifies the type of updates to perform on the bones.

hand_tracker.description: The name of the `XRHandTracker` registered with `XRServer` to obtain the hand tracking data from.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_ANGULAR_VELOCITY_VALID.description: The hand joint's angular velocity data is valid.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_LINEAR_VELOCITY_VALID.description: The hand joint's linear velocity data is valid.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_ORIENTATION_TRACKED.description: The hand joint's orientation is actively tracked. May not be set if tracking has been temporarily lost.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_ORIENTATION_VALID.description: The hand joint's orientation data is valid.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_POSITION_TRACKED.description: The hand joint's position is actively tracked. May not be set if tracking has been temporarily lost.

HAND_JOINT_FLAG_POSITION_VALID.description: The hand joint's position data is valid.

HAND_JOINT_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `HandJoint` enum.

HAND_TRACKING_SOURCE_CONTROLLER.description: The source of hand tracking data is a controller, meaning that joint positions are inferred from controller inputs.

HAND_TRACKING_SOURCE_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `HandTrackingSource` enum.

HAND_TRACKING_SOURCE_NOT_TRACKED.description: No hand tracking data is tracked, this either means the hand is obscured, the controller is turned off, or tracking is not supported for the current input type.

HAND_TRACKING_SOURCE_UNKNOWN.description: The source of hand tracking data is unknown.

HAND_TRACKING_SOURCE_UNOBSTRUCTED.description: The source of hand tracking data is unobstructed, meaning that an accurate method of hand tracking is used. These include optical hand tracking, data gloves, etc.

XRHandTracker.description:
A hand tracking system will create an instance of this object and add it to the `XRServer`. This tracking system will then obtain skeleton data, convert it to the Godot Humanoid hand skeleton and store this data on the `XRHandTracker` object.

Use `XRHandModifier3D` to animate a hand mesh using hand tracking data.

hand_tracking_source.description: The source of the hand tracking data.

has_tracking_data.description: If `true`, the hand tracking data is valid.

XRInterface.brief: Base class for an XR interface implementation.

XR_AR.description: This interface supports AR (video background and real world tracking).

XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ADDITIVE.description: Additive blend mode. This is typically used for AR devices or VR devices with passthrough.

XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND.description: Alpha blend mode. This is typically used for AR or VR devices with passthrough capabilities. The alpha channel controls how much of the passthrough is visible. Alpha of 0.0 means the passthrough is visible and this pixel works in ADDITIVE mode. Alpha of 1.0 means that the passthrough is not visible and this pixel works in OPAQUE mode.

XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_OPAQUE.description: Opaque blend mode. This is typically used for VR devices.

XR_EXCESSIVE_MOTION.description: Tracking is hindered by excessive motion (the player is moving faster than tracking can keep up).

XR_EXTERNAL.description: This interface outputs to an external device. If the main viewport is used, the on screen output is an unmodified buffer of either the left or right eye (stretched if the viewport size is not changed to the same aspect ratio of `get_render_target_size`). Using a separate viewport node frees up the main viewport for other purposes.

XR_INSUFFICIENT_FEATURES.description: Tracking is hindered by insufficient features, it's too dark (for camera-based tracking), player is blocked, etc.

XR_MONO.description: This interface can work with normal rendering output (non-HMD based AR).

XR_NOT_TRACKING.description: Tracking is not functional (camera not plugged in or obscured, lighthouses turned off, etc.).

XR_PLAY_AREA_3DOF.description: Play area only supports orientation tracking, no positional tracking, area will center around player.

XR_PLAY_AREA_CUSTOM.description: Custom play area set by a GDExtension.

XR_PLAY_AREA_ROOMSCALE.description: Player is free to move around, full positional tracking.

XR_PLAY_AREA_SITTING.description: Player is in seated position, limited positional tracking, fixed guardian around player.

XR_PLAY_AREA_STAGE.description: Same as `XR_PLAY_AREA_ROOMSCALE` but origin point is fixed to the center of the physical space. In this mode, system-level recentering may be disabled, requiring the use of `XRServer.center_on_hmd`.

XR_PLAY_AREA_UNKNOWN.description: Play area mode not set or not available.

XR_QUAD.description: This interface supports quad rendering (not yet supported by Godot).

XR_UNKNOWN_TRACKING.description: We don't know the status of the tracking or this interface does not provide feedback.

XR_VRS_TEXTURE_FORMAT_FRAGMENT_DENSITY_M.description: The texture format is the same as expected by the Vulkan `VK_EXT_fragment_density_map` extension.

XR_VRS_TEXTURE_FORMAT_FRAGMENT_SHADING_R.description: The texture format is the same as expected by the Vulkan `VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate` extension.

XR_VRS_TEXTURE_FORMAT_UNIFIED.description: The texture format is the same as returned by `XRVRS.make_vrs_texture`.

XRInterface.description:
This class needs to be implemented to make an AR or VR platform available to Godot and these should be implemented as C++ modules or GDExtension modules. Part of the interface is exposed to GDScript so you can detect, enable and configure an AR or VR platform.

Interfaces should be written in such a way that simply enabling them will give us a working setup. You can query the available interfaces through `XRServer`.

ar_is_anchor_detection_enabled.description: On an AR interface, `true` if anchor detection is enabled.

environment_blend_mode.description: Specify how XR should blend in the environment. This is specific to certain AR and passthrough devices where camera images are blended in by the XR compositor.

interface_is_primary.description: `true` if this is the primary interface.

xr_play_area_mode.description: The play area mode for this interface.

play_area_changed.description: Emitted when the play area is changed. This can be a result of the player resetting the boundary or entering a new play area, the player changing the play area mode, the world scale changing or the player resetting their headset orientation.

XRInterfaceExtension.brief: Base class for XR interface extensions (plugins).
XRInterfaceExtension.description: External XR interface plugins should inherit from this class.

XRNode3D.brief: A 3D node that has its position automatically updated by the `XRServer`.
XRNode3D.description: This node can be bound to a specific pose of an `XRPositionalTracker` and will automatically have its `Node3D.transform` updated by the `XRServer`. Nodes of this type must be added as children of the `XROrigin3D` node.

pose.description:
The name of the pose we're bound to. Which poses a tracker supports is not known during design time.

Godot defines number of standard pose names such as `aim` and `grip` but other may be configured within a given `XRInterface`.

show_when_tracked.description: Enables showing the node when tracking starts, and hiding the node when tracking is lost.

tracker.description:
The name of the tracker we're bound to. Which trackers are available is not known during design time.

Godot defines a number of standard trackers such as `left_hand` and `right_hand` but others may be configured within a given `XRInterface`.

tracking_changed.description: Emitted when the `tracker` starts or stops receiving updated tracking data for the `pose` being tracked. The `tracking` argument indicates whether the tracker is getting updated tracking data.

XROrigin3D.description:
This is a special node within the AR/VR system that maps the physical location of the center of our tracking space to the virtual location within our game world.

Multiple origin points can be added to the scene tree, but only one can used at a time. All the `XRCamera3D`, `XRController3D`, and `XRAnchor3D` nodes should be direct children of this node for spatial tracking to work correctly.

It is the position of this node that you update when your character needs to move through your game world while we're not moving in the real world. Movement in the real world is always in relation to this origin point.

For example, if your character is driving a car, the `XROrigin3D` node should be a child node of this car. Or, if you're implementing a teleport system to move your character, you should change the position of this node.

current.description: If `true`, this origin node is currently being used by the `XRServer`. Only one origin point can be used at a time.

world_scale.description: The scale of the game world compared to the real world. This is the same as `XRServer.world_scale`. By default, most AR/VR platforms assume that 1 game unit corresponds to 1 real world meter.

XRPose.brief: This object contains all data related to a pose on a tracked object.

XR_TRACKING_CONFIDENCE_HIGH.description: Tracking information is considered accurate and up to date.

XR_TRACKING_CONFIDENCE_LOW.description: Tracking information may be inaccurate or estimated. For example, with inside out tracking this would indicate a controller may be (partially) obscured.

XR_TRACKING_CONFIDENCE_NONE.description: No tracking information is available for this pose.

XRPose.description:
XR runtimes often identify multiple locations on devices such as controllers that are spatially tracked.

Orientation, location, linear velocity and angular velocity are all provided for each pose by the XR runtime. This object contains this state of a pose.

angular_velocity.description: The angular velocity for this pose.

has_tracking_data.description: If `true` our tracking data is up to date. If `false` we're no longer receiving new tracking data and our state is whatever that last valid state was.

linear_velocity.description: The linear velocity of this pose.

name.description:
The name of this pose. Usually, this name is derived from an action map set up by the user. Godot also suggests some pose names that `XRInterface` objects are expected to implement:

- `root` is the root location, often used for tracked objects that do not have further nodes.

- `aim` is the tip of a controller with its orientation pointing outwards, often used for raycasts.

- `grip` is the location where the user grips the controller.

- `skeleton` is the root location for a hand mesh, when using hand tracking and an animated skeleton is supplied by the XR runtime.

tracking_confidence.description: The tracking confidence for this pose, provides insight on how accurate the spatial positioning of this record is.

transform.description: The transform containing the original and transform as reported by the XR runtime.

TRACKER_HAND_LEFT.description: This tracker is the left hand controller.

TRACKER_HAND_MAX.description: Represents the size of the `TrackerHand` enum.

TRACKER_HAND_RIGHT.description: This tracker is the right hand controller.

TRACKER_HAND_UNKNOWN.description: The hand this tracker is held in is unknown or not applicable.

XRPositionalTracker.description:
An instance of this object represents a device that is tracked, such as a controller or anchor point. HMDs aren't represented here as they are handled internally.

As controllers are turned on and the `XRInterface` detects them, instances of this object are automatically added to this list of active tracking objects accessible through the `XRServer`.

The `XRNode3D` and `XRAnchor3D` both consume objects of this type and should be used in your project. The positional trackers are just under-the-hood objects that make this all work. These are mostly exposed so that GDExtension-based interfaces can interact with them.

hand.description: Defines which hand this tracker relates to.

profile.description: The profile associated with this tracker, interface dependent but will indicate the type of controller being tracked.

button_pressed.description: Emitted when a button on this tracker is pressed. Note that many XR runtimes allow other inputs to be mapped to buttons.

button_released.description: Emitted when a button on this tracker is released.

input_float_changed.description: Emitted when a trigger or similar input on this tracker changes value.

input_vector2_changed.description: Emitted when a thumbstick or thumbpad on this tracker moves.

pose_changed.description: Emitted when the state of a pose tracked by this tracker changes.

pose_lost_tracking.description: Emitted when a pose tracked by this tracker stops getting updated tracking data.

profile_changed.description: Emitted when the profile of our tracker changes.

XRServer.brief: Server for AR and VR features.

DONT_RESET_ROTATION.description: Does not reset the orientation of the HMD, only the position of the player gets centered.

RESET_BUT_KEEP_TILT.description: Resets the orientation but keeps the tilt of the device. So if we're looking down, we keep looking down but heading will be reset.

RESET_FULL_ROTATION.description: Fully reset the orientation of the HMD. Regardless of what direction the user is looking to in the real world. The user will look dead ahead in the virtual world.

TRACKER_ANCHOR.description: The tracker tracks the location and size of an AR anchor.

TRACKER_ANY.description: Used internally to select all trackers.

TRACKER_ANY_KNOWN.description: Used internally to filter trackers of any known type.

TRACKER_BASESTATION.description: The tracker tracks the location of a base station.

TRACKER_BODY.description: The tracker tracks the location and joints of a body.

TRACKER_CONTROLLER.description: The tracker tracks the location of a controller.

TRACKER_FACE.description: The tracker tracks the expressions of a face.

TRACKER_HAND.description: The tracker tracks the location and joints of a hand.

TRACKER_HEAD.description: The tracker tracks the location of the player's head. This is usually a location centered between the player's eyes. Note that for handheld AR devices this can be the current location of the device.

TRACKER_UNKNOWN.description: Used internally if we haven't set the tracker type yet.

XRServer.description: The AR/VR server is the heart of our Advanced and Virtual Reality solution and handles all the processing.

camera_locked_to_origin.description:
If set to `true`, the scene will be rendered as if the camera is locked to the `XROrigin3D`.

**Note:** This doesn't provide a very comfortable experience for users. This setting exists for doing benchmarking or automated testing, where you want to control what is rendered via code.

primary_interface.description: The primary `XRInterface` currently bound to the `XRServer`.

world_origin.description:
The current origin of our tracking space in the virtual world. This is used by the renderer to properly position the camera with new tracking data.

**Note:** This property is managed by the current `XROrigin3D` node. It is exposed for access from GDExtensions.

world_scale.description: The scale of the game world compared to the real world. By default, most AR/VR platforms assume that 1 game unit corresponds to 1 real world meter.

interface_added.description: Emitted when a new interface has been added.

interface_removed.description: Emitted when an interface is removed.

reference_frame_changed.description: Emitted when the reference frame transform changes.

tracker_added.description: Emitted when a new tracker has been added. If you don't use a fixed number of controllers or if you're using `XRAnchor3D`s for an AR solution, it is important to react to this signal to add the appropriate `XRController3D` or `XRAnchor3D` nodes related to this new tracker.

tracker_removed.description: Emitted when a tracker is removed. You should remove any `XRController3D` or `XRAnchor3D` points if applicable. This is not mandatory, the nodes simply become inactive and will be made active again when a new tracker becomes available (i.e. a new controller is switched on that takes the place of the previous one).

tracker_updated.description: Emitted when an existing tracker has been updated. This can happen if the user switches controllers.

world_origin_changed.description: Emitted when the world origin transform changes.

XRTracker.description: This object is the base of all XR trackers.

name.description:
The unique name of this tracker. The trackers that are available differ between various XR runtimes and can often be configured by the user. Godot maintains a number of reserved names that it expects the `XRInterface` to implement if applicable:

- `"head"` identifies the `XRPositionalTracker` of the player's head

- `"left_hand"` identifies the `XRControllerTracker` in the player's left hand

- `"right_hand"` identifies the `XRControllerTracker` in the player's right hand

- `"/user/hand_tracker/left"` identifies the `XRHandTracker` for the player's left hand

- `"/user/hand_tracker/right"` identifies the `XRHandTracker` for the player's right hand

- `"/user/body_tracker"` identifies the `XRBodyTracker` for the player's body

- `"/user/face_tracker"` identifies the `XRFaceTracker` for the player's face

XRVRS.brief: Helper class for XR interfaces that generates VRS images.
XRVRS.description: This class is used by various XR interfaces to generate VRS textures that can be used to speed up rendering.

vrs_min_radius.description: The minimum radius around the focal point where full quality is guaranteed if VRS is used as a percentage of screen size.

vrs_render_region.description: The render region that the VRS texture will be scaled to when generated.

vrs_strength.description: The strength used to calculate the VRS density map. The greater this value, the more noticeable VRS is.

ZIPPacker.brief: Allows the creation of ZIP files.

APPEND_ADDINZIP.description: Add new files to the existing zip archive at the given path.

APPEND_CREATE.description: Create a new zip archive at the given path.

APPEND_CREATEAFTER.description: Append a new zip archive to the end of the already existing file at the given path.

COMPRESSION_BEST.description: Start a file with the best Deflate compression level (`9`). This is slow to compress, but results in smaller file sizes than `COMPRESSION_DEFAULT`. Decompression speed is generally unaffected by the chosen compression level.

COMPRESSION_DEFAULT.description: Start a file with the default Deflate compression level (`6`). This is a good compromise between speed and file size.

COMPRESSION_FAST.description: Start a file with the fastest Deflate compression level (`1`). This is fast to compress, but results in larger file sizes than `COMPRESSION_DEFAULT`. Decompression speed is generally unaffected by the chosen compression level.

COMPRESSION_NONE.description: Start a file with no compression. This is also known as the "Store" compression mode and is the fastest method of packing files inside a ZIP archive. Consider using this mode for files that are already compressed (such as JPEG, PNG, MP3, or Ogg Vorbis files).

ZIPPacker.description:
This class implements a writer that allows storing the multiple blobs in a ZIP archive. See also `ZIPReader` and `PCKPacker`.

```
# Create a ZIP archive with a single file at its root.
func write_zip_file():
	var writer = ZIPPacker.new()
	var err = writer.open("user://archive.zip")
	if err != OK:
		return err
	writer.start_file("hello.txt")
	writer.write_file("Hello World".to_utf8_buffer())
	writer.close_file()

	writer.close()
	return OK
```

compression_level.description: The compression level used when `start_file` is called. Use `ZIPPacker.CompressionLevel` as a reference.

ZIPReader.brief: Allows reading the content of a ZIP file.
